Pick a pattern

Read the problem for these signals. Most mediums use one pattern, sometimes two (a hash map inside a sliding window, a heap inside a graph search).

Input size hints

The constraints tell you how fast the solution must be. Roughly 108 simple operations run in about a second.

Input sizeAim forUsually means
n ≤ 10O(n!)all permutations
n ≤ 20O(2n)backtracking over subsets, bitmasks
n ≤ 500O(n3)three nested loops, interval DP
n ≤ 5,000O(n2)2D DP, a nested loop
n up to 106O(n log n) or O(n)sorting, heaps, hash maps, two pointers, sliding window, prefix sums
values up to 109O(n log V)binary search on the answer

Solving flow

The same loop works for practice and for the interview itself.

In the room

  1. Ask about the input before you code: its size, whether it's sorted, duplicates, negative numbers, empty input.
  2. Say the brute force first. It shows you understand the problem and gives you a fallback.
  3. Name the pattern and the signal behind it: "contiguous and longest, so a sliding window".
  4. Narrate while you code, and keep helper names honest (CanFinish, Sink, Explore).
  5. Test with a small example of your own, then the edge cases: empty, one element, all equal, negatives.
  6. Finish with time and space complexity, and how you would change the approach if the input grew.
01

Hash map / set

Arrays & strings

Use it when you need a pair or complement, ask "have I seen this before?", count frequencies, spot duplicates, or group items that share a key.

How it works

  • Trade memory for time: O(1) lookups turn "check every pair" (O(n²)) into one pass.
  • Store what you've seen. For each new item, ask whether its partner is already stored.
  • To group things, compute a canonical key (sorted letters, a count signature) and bucket by it.

Watch out

  • Look for the partner before storing the current item, so nothing pairs with itself.
  • Look up and handle the miss in one call rather than checking for the key and then indexing: one lookup, no exception.

Two Sum#1Easy

Return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target.

function twoSum(nums: number[], target: number): number[] {
  const seen = new Map<number, number>();  // value -> index

  for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
    const j = seen.get(target - nums[i]);
    if (j !== undefined) return [j, i];  // partner seen earlier

    seen.set(nums[i], i);  // store after checking
  }

  return [];
}
def two_sum(nums: list[int], target: int) -> list[int]:
    seen: dict[int, int] = {}                  # value -> index

    for i, num in enumerate(nums):
        if target - num in seen:
            return [seen[target - num], i]     # partner was seen earlier

        seen[num] = i                          # store after checking

    return []
public int[] twoSum(int[] nums, int target) {
    Map<Integer, Integer> seen = new HashMap<>();  // value -> index

    for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
        Integer j = seen.get(target - nums[i]);
        if (j != null)
            return new int[] {j, i};               // partner was seen earlier

        seen.put(nums[i], i);                      // store after checking
    }

    return new int[0];
}
public int[] TwoSum(int[] nums, int target)
{
    var seen = new Dictionary<int, int>();       // value -> index

    for (int i = 0; i < nums.Length; i++)
    {
        if (seen.TryGetValue(target - nums[i], out int j))
            return [j, i];                       // partner was seen earlier

        seen[nums[i]] = i;                       // store after checking
    }

    return [];
}
let twoSum (nums: int[]) (target: int) : int[] =
    let seen = Dictionary<int, int>()            // value -> index

    let rec loop i =
        if i = nums.Length then [||]
        else
            match seen.TryGetValue(target - nums[i]) with
            | true, j -> [| j; i |]              // partner was seen earlier
            | _ ->
                seen[nums[i]] <- i               // store after checking
                loop (i + 1)

    loop 0
vector<int> twoSum(vector<int>& nums, int target)
{
    unordered_map<int, int> seen;                  // value -> index

    for (int i = 0; i < (int)nums.size(); i++)
    {
        auto it = seen.find(target - nums[i]);
        if (it != seen.end())
            return {it->second, i};                // partner was seen earlier

        seen[nums[i]] = i;                         // store after checking
    }

    return {};
}
func twoSum(nums []int, target int) []int {
	seen := map[int]int{} // value -> index

	for i, num := range nums {
		if j, ok := seen[target-num]; ok {
			return []int{j, i} // partner was seen earlier
		}

		seen[num] = i // store after checking
	}

	return []int{}
}
pub fn two_sum(nums: &[i32], target: i32) -> Vec<i32> {
    let mut seen = HashMap::new();               // value -> index

    for (i, &num) in nums.iter().enumerate() {
        if let Some(&j) = seen.get(&(target - num)) {
            return vec![j as i32, i as i32];     // partner was seen earlier
        }

        seen.insert(num, i);                     // store after checking
    }

    Vec::new()
}

Time O(n) · Space O(n)

Group Anagrams#49Medium

Group the words that are anagrams of each other.

function groupAnagrams(strs: string[]): string[][] {
  const groups = new Map<string, string[]>();

  for (const word of strs) {
    const key = [...word].sort().join("");  // "eat", "tea" -> "aet"

    const group = groups.get(key);
    if (group) group.push(word);
    else groups.set(key, [word]);
  }

  return [...groups.values()];
}
def group_anagrams(strs: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:
    groups: defaultdict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)

    for word in strs:
        key = "".join(sorted(word))            # "eat", "tea", "ate" -> "aet"
        groups[key].append(word)

    return list(groups.values())
public List<List<String>> groupAnagrams(String[] strs) {
    Map<String, List<String>> groups = new HashMap<>();

    for (String word : strs) {
        char[] letters = word.toCharArray();
        Arrays.sort(letters);
        String key = new String(letters);          // "eat", "tea", "ate" -> "aet"

        groups.computeIfAbsent(key, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(word);
    }

    return new ArrayList<>(groups.values());
}
public IList<IList<string>> GroupAnagrams(string[] strs)
{
    var groups = new Dictionary<string, IList<string>>();

    foreach (string word in strs)
    {
        char[] letters = word.ToCharArray();
        Array.Sort(letters);
        string key = new string(letters);        // "eat", "tea", "ate" -> "aet"

        if (!groups.TryGetValue(key, out var group))
            groups[key] = group = new List<string>();

        group.Add(word);
    }

    return groups.Values.ToList();
}
let groupAnagrams (strs: string[]) : IList<IList<string>> =
    let groups = Dictionary<string, IList<string>>()

    for word in strs do
        let key = String(word |> Seq.sort |> Seq.toArray)   // "eat", "tea", "ate" -> "aet"

        match groups.TryGetValue key with
        | true, group -> group.Add word
        | _ -> groups[key] <- ResizeArray<string>([ word ]) :> IList<string>

    groups.Values |> Seq.toArray :> IList<IList<string>>
vector<vector<string>> groupAnagrams(vector<string>& strs)
{
    unordered_map<string, vector<string>> groups;

    for (string& word : strs)
    {
        string key = word;
        sort(key.begin(), key.end());              // "eat", "tea", "ate" -> "aet"

        groups[key].push_back(word);
    }

    vector<vector<string>> result;
    for (auto& entry : groups)
        result.push_back(move(entry.second));

    return result;
}
func groupAnagrams(strs []string) [][]string {
	groups := map[string][]string{}

	for _, word := range strs {
		letters := []byte(word)
		sort.Slice(letters, func(i, j int) bool { return letters[i] < letters[j] })
		key := string(letters) // "eat", "tea", "ate" -> "aet"

		groups[key] = append(groups[key], word) // append to a missing key just works
	}

	result := make([][]string, 0, len(groups))
	for _, group := range groups {
		result = append(result, group)
	}
	return result
}
pub fn group_anagrams(strs: &[String]) -> Vec<Vec<String>> {
    let mut groups: HashMap<String, Vec<String>> = HashMap::new();

    for word in strs {
        let mut letters: Vec<u8> = word.bytes().collect();
        letters.sort_unstable();
        let key = String::from_utf8(letters).unwrap();   // "eat", "tea", "ate" -> "aet"

        groups.entry(key).or_default().push(word.clone());
    }

    groups.into_values().collect()
}

Time O(n · k log k) for n words of length k · Space O(n · k)

02

Two pointers

Arrays & strings

Use it when the array is sorted (or you're allowed to sort it), you need a pair or triplet that hits a target, you're checking a palindrome, or you must reverse or partition in place.

How it works

  • Start one pointer at each end. Sum too small: move left right. Too big: move right left.
  • Each step discards one element permanently, so the scan is O(n) instead of O(n²).
  • Same-direction variant: a slow "write" pointer and a fast "read" pointer filter an array in place.

Watch out

  • Sorting costs O(n log n) and loses the original indices. If you must return indices from unsorted input, use a hash map.
  • For unique results, skip equal neighbors after you use a value.

Two Sum II: Input Array Is Sorted#167Medium

The array is sorted and 1-indexed. Return the two positions that add up to target using O(1) extra space.

function twoSum(numbers: number[], target: number): number[] {
  let left = 0, right = numbers.length - 1;

  while (left < right) {
    const sum = numbers[left] + numbers[right];

    if (sum === target) return [left + 1, right + 1];  // 1-indexed
    if (sum < target) left++;                          // too small
    else right--;                                      // too big
  }

  return [];
}
def two_sum(numbers: list[int], target: int) -> list[int]:
    left, right = 0, len(numbers) - 1

    while left < right:
        total = numbers[left] + numbers[right]

        if total == target:
            return [left + 1, right + 1]       # 1-indexed
        if total < target:
            left += 1                          # too small: only a bigger left value helps
        else:
            right -= 1                         # too big: only a smaller right value helps

    return []
public int[] twoSum(int[] numbers, int target) {
    int left = 0, right = numbers.length - 1;

    while (left < right) {
        int sum = numbers[left] + numbers[right];

        if (sum == target) return new int[] {left + 1, right + 1};   // 1-indexed
        if (sum < target) left++;     // too small: only a bigger left value helps
        else right--;                 // too big: only a smaller right value helps
    }

    return new int[0];
}
public int[] TwoSum(int[] numbers, int target)
{
    int left = 0, right = numbers.Length - 1;

    while (left < right)
    {
        int sum = numbers[left] + numbers[right];

        if (sum == target) return [left + 1, right + 1];   // 1-indexed
        if (sum < target) left++;    // too small: only a bigger left value helps
        else right--;                // too big: only a smaller right value helps
    }

    return [];
}
let twoSum (numbers: int[]) (target: int) : int[] =
    let mutable left = 0
    let mutable right = numbers.Length - 1
    let mutable answer = [||]

    while answer.Length = 0 && left < right do
        let sum = numbers[left] + numbers[right]

        if sum = target then answer <- [| left + 1; right + 1 |]   // 1-indexed
        elif sum < target then left <- left + 1    // too small: only a bigger left value helps
        else right <- right - 1                    // too big: only a smaller right value helps

    answer
vector<int> twoSum(vector<int>& numbers, int target)
{
    int left = 0, right = (int)numbers.size() - 1;

    while (left < right)
    {
        int sum = numbers[left] + numbers[right];

        if (sum == target) return {left + 1, right + 1};   // 1-indexed
        if (sum < target) left++;                  // too small: only a bigger left value helps
        else right--;                              // too big: only a smaller right value helps
    }

    return {};
}
func twoSum(numbers []int, target int) []int {
	left, right := 0, len(numbers)-1

	for left < right {
		sum := numbers[left] + numbers[right]

		if sum == target {
			return []int{left + 1, right + 1} // 1-indexed
		}
		if sum < target {
			left++ // too small: only a bigger left value helps
		} else {
			right-- // too big: only a smaller right value helps
		}
	}

	return []int{}
}
pub fn two_sum(numbers: &[i32], target: i32) -> Vec<i32> {
    let (mut left, mut right) = (0, numbers.len() - 1);

    while left < right {
        let sum = numbers[left] + numbers[right];

        if sum == target {
            return vec![left as i32 + 1, right as i32 + 1];   // 1-indexed
        }

        if sum < target {
            left += 1;                           // too small: only a bigger left value helps
        } else {
            right -= 1;                          // too big: only a smaller right value helps
        }
    }

    Vec::new()
}

Time O(n) · Space O(1)

3Sum#15Medium

Return every unique triplet that sums to zero. Fix one number, then run Two Sum II on the rest.

function threeSum(nums: number[]): number[][] {
  nums.sort((a, b) => a - b);  // as numbers, not as text
  const result: number[][] = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < nums.length - 2; i++) {
    if (i > 0 && nums[i] === nums[i - 1]) continue;  // same anchor

    let left = i + 1, right = nums.length - 1;
    while (left < right) {
      const sum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right];

      if (sum < 0) left++;
      else if (sum > 0) right--;
      else {
        result.push([nums[i], nums[left], nums[right]]);
        left++;
        right--;
        while (left < right && nums[left] === nums[left - 1])
          left++;  // skip repeated values
      }
    }
  }

  return result;
}
def three_sum(nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
    nums.sort()
    result: list[list[int]] = []

    for i in range(len(nums) - 2):
        if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]:
            continue                           # same anchor, same triplets

        left, right = i + 1, len(nums) - 1
        while left < right:
            total = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right]

            if total < 0:
                left += 1
            elif total > 0:
                right -= 1
            else:
                result.append([nums[i], nums[left], nums[right]])
                left += 1
                right -= 1
                while left < right and nums[left] == nums[left - 1]:
                    left += 1                  # skip repeated values

    return result
public List<List<Integer>> threeSum(int[] nums) {
    Arrays.sort(nums);
    List<List<Integer>> result = new ArrayList<>();

    for (int i = 0; i < nums.length - 2; i++) {
        if (i > 0 && nums[i] == nums[i - 1]) continue;   // same anchor, same triplets

        int left = i + 1, right = nums.length - 1;
        while (left < right) {
            int sum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right];

            if (sum < 0) left++;
            else if (sum > 0) right--;
            else {
                result.add(List.of(nums[i], nums[left], nums[right]));
                left++;
                right--;
                while (left < right && nums[left] == nums[left - 1])
                    left++;                            // skip repeated values
            }
        }
    }

    return result;
}
public IList<IList<int>> ThreeSum(int[] nums)
{
    Array.Sort(nums);
    var result = new List<IList<int>>();

    for (int i = 0; i < nums.Length - 2; i++)
    {
        if (i > 0 && nums[i] == nums[i - 1]) continue;   // same anchor, same triplets

        int left = i + 1, right = nums.Length - 1;
        while (left < right)
        {
            int sum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right];

            if (sum < 0) left++;
            else if (sum > 0) right--;
            else
            {
                result.Add([nums[i], nums[left], nums[right]]);
                left++;
                right--;
                while (left < right && nums[left] == nums[left - 1])
                    left++;                               // skip repeated values
            }
        }
    }

    return result;
}
let threeSum (nums: int[]) : IList<IList<int>> =
    Array.sortInPlace nums
    let result = ResizeArray<IList<int>>()

    for i in 0 .. nums.Length - 3 do
        if i = 0 || nums[i] <> nums[i - 1] then     // same anchor, same triplets
            let mutable left = i + 1
            let mutable right = nums.Length - 1

            while left < right do
                let sum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right]

                if sum < 0 then left <- left + 1
                elif sum > 0 then right <- right - 1
                else
                    result.Add([| nums[i]; nums[left]; nums[right] |] :> IList<int>)
                    left <- left + 1
                    right <- right - 1
                    while left < right && nums[left] = nums[left - 1] do
                        left <- left + 1                // skip repeated values

    result :> IList<IList<int>>
vector<vector<int>> threeSum(vector<int>& nums)
{
    sort(nums.begin(), nums.end());
    vector<vector<int>> result;

    for (int i = 0; i < (int)nums.size() - 2; i++)
    {
        if (i > 0 && nums[i] == nums[i - 1]) continue;   // same anchor, same triplets

        int left = i + 1, right = (int)nums.size() - 1;
        while (left < right)
        {
            int sum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right];

            if (sum < 0) left++;
            else if (sum > 0) right--;
            else
            {
                result.push_back({nums[i], nums[left], nums[right]});
                left++;
                right--;
                while (left < right && nums[left] == nums[left - 1])
                    left++;                        // skip repeated values
            }
        }
    }

    return result;
}
func threeSum(nums []int) [][]int {
	sort.Ints(nums)
	result := [][]int{}

	for i := 0; i < len(nums)-2; i++ {
		if i > 0 && nums[i] == nums[i-1] {
			continue // same anchor, same triplets
		}

		left, right := i+1, len(nums)-1
		for left < right {
			sum := nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right]

			if sum < 0 {
				left++
			} else if sum > 0 {
				right--
			} else {
				result = append(result, []int{nums[i], nums[left], nums[right]})
				left++
				right--
				for left < right && nums[left] == nums[left-1] {
					left++ // skip repeated values
				}
			}
		}
	}

	return result
}
pub fn three_sum(nums: &[i32]) -> Vec<Vec<i32>> {
    let mut nums = nums.to_vec();
    nums.sort_unstable();
    let mut result = Vec::new();

    for i in 0..nums.len().saturating_sub(2) {
        if i > 0 && nums[i] == nums[i - 1] { continue; }   // same anchor, same triplets

        let (mut left, mut right) = (i + 1, nums.len() - 1);
        while left < right {
            let sum = nums[i] + nums[left] + nums[right];

            if sum < 0 { left += 1; }
            else if sum > 0 { right -= 1; }
            else {
                result.push(vec![nums[i], nums[left], nums[right]]);
                left += 1;
                right -= 1;
                while left < right && nums[left] == nums[left - 1] {
                    left += 1;                   // skip repeated values
                }
            }
        }
    }

    result
}

Time O(n²) · Space O(1) beyond the output

03

Sliding window

Arrays & strings

Use it when you want the longest, shortest or number of contiguous subarrays or substrings that follow a rule: no repeats, at most K distinct, a sum of at least the target.

How it works

  • Move right one step at a time and add the new element to the window's state (a set, counts, a sum).
  • When the window breaks the rule, move left until it's valid again.
  • Every index enters and leaves once, so it's O(n) despite the nested loop.

Watch out

  • Longest: shrink while invalid, then record. Shortest: record while valid, then shrink.
  • Shrinking must be able to fix the window. With negative numbers it can't, so use prefix sums.

Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters#3Mediumdojo 03

The length of the longest substring with no repeated characters.

function lengthOfLongestSubstring(s: string): number {
  const inWindow = new Set<string>();
  let left = 0, best = 0;

  for (let right = 0; right < s.length; right++) {
    while (inWindow.has(s[right]))  // invalid: shrink from the left
      inWindow.delete(s[left++]);

    inWindow.add(s[right]);  // grow on the right
    best = Math.max(best, right - left + 1);
  }

  return best;
}
def length_of_longest_substring(s: str) -> int:
    window: set[str] = set()
    left = 0
    best = 0

    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        while ch in window:                    # invalid: shrink from the left
            window.remove(s[left])
            left += 1

        window.add(ch)                         # grow on the right
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)

    return best
public int lengthOfLongestSubstring(String s) {
    Set<Character> window = new HashSet<>();
    int left = 0, best = 0;

    for (int right = 0; right < s.length(); right++) {
        while (window.contains(s.charAt(right)))   // invalid: shrink from the left
            window.remove(s.charAt(left++));

        window.add(s.charAt(right));               // grow on the right
        best = Math.max(best, right - left + 1);
    }

    return best;
}
public int LengthOfLongestSubstring(string s)
{
    var window = new HashSet<char>();
    int left = 0, best = 0;

    for (int right = 0; right < s.Length; right++)
    {
        while (window.Contains(s[right]))        // invalid: shrink from the left
            window.Remove(s[left++]);

        window.Add(s[right]);                    // grow on the right
        best = Math.Max(best, right - left + 1);
    }

    return best;
}
let lengthOfLongestSubstring (s: string) : int =
    let window = HashSet<char>()
    let mutable left = 0
    let mutable best = 0

    for right in 0 .. s.Length - 1 do
        while window.Contains s[right] do       // invalid: shrink from the left
            window.Remove(s[left]) |> ignore
            left <- left + 1

        window.Add s[right] |> ignore           // grow on the right
        best <- max best (right - left + 1)

    best
int lengthOfLongestSubstring(string s)
{
    unordered_set<char> window;
    int left = 0, best = 0;

    for (int right = 0; right < (int)s.size(); right++)
    {
        while (window.count(s[right]))             // invalid: shrink from the left
            window.erase(s[left++]);

        window.insert(s[right]);                   // grow on the right
        best = max(best, right - left + 1);
    }

    return best;
}
func lengthOfLongestSubstring(s string) int {
	window := map[byte]bool{}
	left, best := 0, 0

	for right := 0; right < len(s); right++ {
		for window[s[right]] { // invalid: shrink from the left
			delete(window, s[left])
			left++
		}

		window[s[right]] = true // grow on the right
		best = max(best, right-left+1)
	}

	return best
}
pub fn length_of_longest_substring(s: &str) -> i32 {
    let bytes = s.as_bytes();
    let mut window = HashSet::new();
    let (mut left, mut best) = (0, 0);

    for (right, &ch) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {
        while window.contains(&ch) {             // invalid: shrink from the left
            window.remove(&bytes[left]);
            left += 1;
        }

        window.insert(ch);                       // grow on the right
        best = best.max(right - left + 1);
    }

    best as i32
}

Time O(n) · Space O(size of the alphabet)

Minimum Size Subarray Sum#209Medium

The length of the shortest subarray whose sum is at least target (0 if none). All numbers are positive.

function minSubArrayLen(target: number, nums: number[]): number {
  let left = 0, sum = 0, best = Infinity;

  for (let right = 0; right < nums.length; right++) {
    sum += nums[right];

    while (sum >= target) {  // valid: record, then try shorter
      best = Math.min(best, right - left + 1);
      sum -= nums[left++];
    }
  }

  return best === Infinity ? 0 : best;
}

        total += num

        while total >= target:                 # valid: record, then try shorter
            best = min(best, right - left + 1)
            total -= nums[left]
            left += 1

    return 0 if best == float("inf") else int(best)

			best = min(best, right-left+1)

        sum += num;

        while sum >= target {                    // valid: record, then try shorter
            best = best.min(right - left + 1);
            sum -= nums[left];
            left += 1;
        }
    }

    if best == usize::MAX { 0 } else { best as i32 }

04

Prefix sum

Arrays & strings

Use it when you need sums over ranges, "subarray sums to K", "equal numbers of 0s and 1s", many range queries on data that doesn't change, or negative numbers rule out a sliding window.

How it works

  • prefix[i] is the sum of the first i numbers, one slot longer than the input.
  • The sum of nums[i..j] is prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i].
  • Two equal prefix sums mean the numbers between them sum to 0 (if they differ by K, to K). Keep the sums in a hash map to find these ranges in one pass.

Watch out

  • Seed the map with the empty prefix (sum 0 at index -1, or a count of 1) so ranges that start at index 0 count.
  • Large inputs can overflow int; use long sums.

Range Sum Query: Immutable#303Easy

Answer many "sum of nums[left..right]" queries quickly.

class NumArray {
  private prefix: number[];  // prefix[i] = sum of the first i

  constructor(nums: number[]) {
    this.prefix = new Array(nums.length + 1).fill(0);
    for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++)
      this.prefix[i + 1] = this.prefix[i] + nums[i];
  }

  sumRange(left: number, right: number): number {
    return this.prefix[right + 1] - this.prefix[left];
  }
}

        for i, num in enumerate(nums):
            self.prefix[i + 1] = self.prefix[i] + num

    def sum_range(self, left: int, right: int) -> int:
        return self.prefix[right + 1] - self.prefix[left]

    public NumArray(int[] nums) {
        prefix = new int[nums.length + 1];
        for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++)
            prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i];
    }

    public int sumRange(int left, int right) {
        return prefix[right + 1] - prefix[left];
    }
}

func newNumArray(nums []int) NumArray {

        for i in 0..nums.len() {
            prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i];
        }
        NumArray { prefix }
    }

    pub fn sum_range(&self, left: i32, right: i32) -> i32 {
        self.prefix[right as usize + 1] - self.prefix[left as usize]
    }
}

Contiguous Array#525Medium

The length of the longest subarray with equal numbers of 0s and 1s.

function findMaxLength(nums: number[]): number {
  const firstSeen = new Map([[0, -1]]);  // sum -> first index
  let sum = 0, best = 0;

  for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
    sum += nums[i] === 1 ? 1 : -1;  // a 0 counts as -1

    const start = firstSeen.get(sum);
    if (start !== undefined)
      best = Math.max(best, i - start);  // same sum: the gap sums to 0
    else
      firstSeen.set(sum, i);             // keep the earliest
  }

  return best;
}
def find_max_length(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    first_seen = {0: -1}                       # sum -> first index
    total, best = 0, 0

    for i, num in enumerate(nums):
        total += 1 if num == 1 else -1         # a 0 counts as -1, so balanced = 0

        if total in first_seen:
            best = max(best, i - first_seen[total])  # same sum again: the gap sums to 0
        else:
            first_seen[total] = i              # keep the earliest for the longest gap

    return best
public int findMaxLength(int[] nums) {
    Map<Integer, Integer> firstSeen = new HashMap<>();   // sum -> first index
    firstSeen.put(0, -1);
    int sum = 0, best = 0;

    for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
        sum += nums[i] == 1 ? 1 : -1;           // a 0 counts as -1, so balanced = 0

        Integer start = firstSeen.get(sum);
        if (start != null)
            best = Math.max(best, i - start);   // same sum again: the gap sums to 0
        else
            firstSeen.put(sum, i);              // keep the earliest for the longest gap
    }

    return best;
}

{

    int sum = 0, best = 0;

    {
        sum += nums[i] == 1 ? 1 : -1;            // a 0 counts as -1, so balanced = 0

        if (firstSeen.TryGetValue(sum, out int start))
            best = Math.Max(best, i - start);    // same sum again: the gap sums to 0
        else
            firstSeen[sum] = i;                  // keep the earliest for the longest gap
    }

    return best;
}

    let firstSeen = Dictionary<int, int>()      // sum -> first index
    firstSeen[0] <- -1
    let mutable sum = 0
    let mutable best = 0

    for i in 0 .. nums.Length - 1 do
        sum <- sum + (if nums[i] = 1 then 1 else -1)   // a 0 counts as -1, so balanced = 0

        match firstSeen.TryGetValue sum with
        | true, start -> best <- max best (i - start)  // same sum again: the gap sums to 0
        | _ -> firstSeen[sum] <- i                     // keep the earliest for the longest gap

    best
int findMaxLength(vector<int>& nums)
{
    unordered_map<int, int> firstSeen{{0, -1}};    // sum -> first index
    int sum = 0, best = 0;

    for (int i = 0; i < (int)nums.size(); i++)
    {
        sum += nums[i] == 1 ? 1 : -1;              // a 0 counts as -1, so balanced = 0

        auto it = firstSeen.find(sum);
        if (it != firstSeen.end())
            best = max(best, i - it->second);      // same sum again: the gap sums to 0
        else
            firstSeen[sum] = i;                    // keep the earliest for the longest gap
    }

    return best;
}
func findMaxLength(nums []int) int {
	firstSeen := map[int]int{0: -1} // sum -> first index
	sum, best := 0, 0

	for i, num := range nums {
		if num == 1 {
			sum++
		} else {
			sum-- // a 0 counts as -1, so balanced = 0
		}

		if start, ok := firstSeen[sum]; ok {
			best = max(best, i-start) // same sum again: the gap sums to 0
		} else {
			firstSeen[sum] = i // keep the earliest for the longest gap
		}
	}

	return best
}
pub fn find_max_length(nums: &[i32]) -> i32 {
    let mut first_seen = HashMap::new();         // sum -> first index
    first_seen.insert(0, -1);                    // sum 0 is "seen" before the array
    let (mut sum, mut best) = (0, 0);

    for (i, &num) in nums.iter().enumerate() {
        sum += if num == 1 { 1 } else { -1 };    // a 0 counts as -1, so balanced = 0

        if let Some(&start) = first_seen.get(&sum) {
            best = best.max(i as i32 - start);   // same sum again: the gap sums to 0
        } else {
            first_seen.insert(sum, i as i32);    // keep the earliest for the longest gap
        }
    }

    best
}

Time O(n) · Space O(n)

05

Binary search

Arrays & strings

Use it when the input is sorted or rotated, you need the first or last position of something, O(log n) is required, or the question is "the minimum X that works" or "maximize the minimum" (binary search on the answer).

How it works

  • Keep a range [lo, hi] that must contain the answer, and halve it each step.
  • Phrase every problem as "the first index where the condition is true", then always use one template: if (Condition(mid)) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1;
  • On the answer: if you can check a candidate in O(n), and the check is monotonic (works for x, so works for x + 1), search the candidates instead of the array.

Watch out

  • Write lo + (hi - lo) / 2 so the midpoint can't overflow.
  • With while (lo < hi) and hi = mid, never write lo = mid: it can loop forever.

Search Insert Position#35Easy

The index of target in a sorted array, or where it would be inserted. This is the lower-bound template.

function searchInsert(nums: number[], target: number): number {
  let lo = 0, hi = nums.length;  // the answer is in [lo, hi]

  while (lo < hi) {
    const mid = Math.floor((lo + hi) / 2);
    if (nums[mid] < target) lo = mid + 1;  // the answer is right of mid
    else hi = mid;                         // mid could be the answer
  }

  return lo;  // the first index with nums[i] >= target
}
def search_insert(nums: list[int], target: int) -> int:
    lo, hi = 0, len(nums)                      # the answer is in [lo, hi]

    while lo < hi:
        mid = lo + (hi - lo) // 2
        if nums[mid] < target:
            lo = mid + 1                       # mid too small: answer is right of it
        else:
            hi = mid                           # mid could be the answer: keep it

    return lo                                  # first index with nums[i] >= target

Koko Eating Bananas#875Medium

The slowest eating speed that finishes every pile within h hours.

function minEatingSpeed(piles: number[], h: number): number {
  let lo = 1, hi = Math.max(...piles);  // search speeds, not the array

  while (lo < hi) {
    const mid = Math.floor((lo + hi) / 2);
    if (canFinish(piles, h, mid)) hi = mid;  // works: try slower
    else lo = mid + 1;                       // too slow: go faster
  }

  return lo;
}

function canFinish(piles: number[], h: number, speed: number): boolean {
  let hours = 0;
  for (const pile of piles)
    hours += Math.ceil(pile / speed);  // a part hour is a whole hour
  return hours <= h;
}

        if can_finish(piles, h, mid):
            hi = mid                           # works: try slower
        else:
            lo = mid + 1                       # too slow: go faster

    return lo

    let mut hours: i64 = 0;
    for &pile in piles {

    }
    hours <= h as i64
}

06

Stack / monotonic stack

Data structures

Use it when you see matching brackets, nested structure (decoding, calculators), undoing the most recent thing, or "the next (or previous) greater or smaller element".

How it works

  • A stack keeps what's still open, newest on top.
  • Monotonic stack: keep entries in sorted order. A new element pops everything it beats, and each pop settles that entry's answer.
  • Every element is pushed and popped at most once: O(n) overall.

Watch out

  • Push indices instead of values when you need distances between positions.
  • Check Count > 0 before Peek or Pop.

Valid Parentheses#20Easy

Are the brackets balanced and correctly nested?

function isValid(s: string): boolean {
  const expected: string[] = [];  // closers we still owe

  for (const c of s) {
    if (c === "(") expected.push(")");
    else if (c === "[") expected.push("]");
    else if (c === "{") expected.push("}");
    else if (expected.pop() !== c) return false;  // wrong, or none
  }

  return expected.length === 0;
}

            expected.append("]")
        elif c == "{":
            expected.append("}")
        elif not expected or expected.pop() != c:
            return False

    return not expected

        else if (c == '[') expected.push(']');
        else if (c == '{') expected.push('}');

        match ch {
            '(' => expected.push(')'),
            '[' => expected.push(']'),
            '{' => expected.push('}'),
            _ => {
                if expected.pop() != Some(ch) {
                    return false;                // empty stack or wrong closer
                }
            }
        }
    }

    expected.is_empty()
}

Online Stock Span#901Medium

For each new price, how many consecutive days (today included) had a price no higher than today's?

class StockSpanner {
  // [price, span] pairs; prices fall from the bottom to the top
  private stack: [number, number][] = [];

  next(price: number): number {
    const stack = this.stack;
    let span = 1;
    while (stack.length > 0 && stack[stack.length - 1][0] <= price)
      span += stack.pop()![1];  // cover the days it covered

    stack.push([price, span]);
    return span;
  }
}
class StockSpanner:
    def __init__(self):
        # Prices strictly decrease from the bottom of the stack to the top.
        self.stack: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

    def next(self, price: int) -> int:
        span = 1
        while self.stack and self.stack[-1][0] <= price:
            span += self.stack.pop()[1]        # today also covers the days it covered

        self.stack.append((price, span))
        return span
public class StockSpanner {
    // Entries are {price, span}; prices strictly decrease from the bottom to the top.
    private final Deque<int[]> stack = new ArrayDeque<>();

    public int next(int price) {
        int span = 1;
        while (!stack.isEmpty() && stack.peek()[0] <= price)
            span += stack.pop()[1];            // today also covers the days it covered

        stack.push(new int[] {price, span});
        return span;
    }
}

func (s *StockSpanner) next(price int) int {
	span := 1
	for len(s.stack) > 0 && s.stack[len(s.stack)-1][0] <= price {
		span += s.stack[len(s.stack)-1][1] // today also covers the days it covered
		s.stack = s.stack[:len(s.stack)-1]
	}

	s.stack = append(s.stack, [2]int{price, span})
	return span
}
pub struct StockSpanner {

impl StockSpanner {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        StockSpanner { stack: Vec::new() }
    }

    pub fn next(&mut self, price: i32) -> i32 {
        let mut span = 1;
        while let Some(&(top_price, top_span)) = self.stack.last() {
            if top_price > price { break; }
            span += top_span;                    // today also covers the days it covered
            self.stack.pop();
        }

        self.stack.push((price, span));
        span
    }
}

07

Linked list

Data structures

Use it when the input is a ListNode and you must reverse, reorder or merge it, or find its middle, a cycle, or the kth node from the end, usually in O(1) extra space.

How it works

  • Dummy head: a fake node before head, so inserting or deleting at the front isn't a special case.
  • Fast and slow pointers: fast moves two steps, slow one. They find the middle, detect a cycle, or (with a head start of n) the nth from the end.
  • Reverse in place with prev, cur and next, flipping one arrow per step.

Watch out

  • Save cur.next before you overwrite it.
  • Draw a three-node list first. Most bugs are null checks at the ends.

Toolkit: Reverse Linked List#206 and Middle of the Linked List#876Easy

The two moves most list mediums are built from. Reorder List (#143) is exactly these two plus a merge.

// Reverse in place: point each node back at the one before it.
function reverseList(head: ListNode | null): ListNode | null {
  let prev: ListNode | null = null, cur = head;

  while (cur !== null) {
    const next = cur.next;  // save it before rewiring
    cur.next = prev;
    prev = cur;
    cur = next;
  }

  return prev;
}

// Fast and slow: fast takes two steps for each step of slow.
function middleNode(head: ListNode | null): ListNode | null {
  let slow = head, fast = head;

  while (fast !== null && fast.next !== null) {
    slow = slow!.next;  // behind fast, so never null
    fast = fast.next.next;
  }

  return slow;
}
# Reverse in place: point each node back at the one before it.
def reverse_list(head: ListNode | None) -> ListNode | None:
    prev, cur = None, head

    while cur:
        nxt = cur.next                         # save it before rewiring
        cur.next = prev
        prev = cur
        cur = nxt

    return prev


# Fast and slow: fast takes two steps for each step of slow, so slow stops mid-list.
def middle_node(head: ListNode | None) -> ListNode | None:
    slow = fast = head

    while fast and fast.next:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next

    return slow
// Reverse in place: point each node back at the one before it.

        cur.next = prev;

        slow = slow.next;
        fast = fast.next.next;
    }

    return slow;
}

func reverseList(head *ListNode) *ListNode {
	var prev *ListNode
	cur := head

	for cur != nil {
		next := cur.Next // save it before rewiring
		cur.Next = prev
		prev = cur
		cur = next
	}

	return prev
}

// Fast and slow: fast takes two steps for each step of slow, so slow stops mid-list.

	slow, fast := head, head

	for fast != nil && fast.Next != nil {
		slow = slow.Next
		fast = fast.Next.Next
	}

	return slow

// Reverse in place: point each node back at the one before it.
pub fn reverse_list(head: ListLink) -> ListLink {
    let mut prev: ListLink = None;
    let mut cur = head;

    while let Some(mut node) = cur {
        cur = node.next.take();                  // save it before rewiring
        node.next = prev;
        prev = Some(node);
    }

    prev
}

// Fast and slow: fast takes two steps for each step of slow, so slow stops mid-list.
pub fn middle_node(head: ListLink) -> ListLink {
    // A Box list cannot be shared, so record where slow stops and walk there once.
    let mut steps = 0;
    let mut fast = &head;

    while fast.is_some() && fast.as_ref().unwrap().next.is_some() {
        steps += 1;
        fast = &fast.as_ref().unwrap().next.as_ref().unwrap().next;
    }

    let mut slow = head;
    for _ in 0..steps {
        slow = slow.and_then(|node| node.next);
    }

    slow
}

Remove Nth Node From End of List#19Medium

Remove the nth node from the end in a single pass.

function removeNthFromEnd(
  head: ListNode | null,
  n: number,
): ListNode | null {
  const dummy = new ListNode(0, head);  // lets us delete the head too
  let fast: ListNode = dummy, slow: ListNode = dummy;

  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++)
    fast = fast.next!;  // open a gap of n nodes

  while (fast.next !== null) {  // until fast is the tail
    fast = fast.next;
    slow = slow.next!;
  }

  slow.next = slow.next!.next;  // slow sits just before the target
  return dummy.next;
}
def remove_nth_from_end(head: ListNode | None, n: int) -> ListNode | None:
    dummy = ListNode(0, head)                  # lets us delete the real head too
    fast = slow = dummy

    for _ in range(n):
        fast = fast.next                       # open a gap of n nodes

    while fast.next:                           # move both until fast is the tail
        fast = fast.next
        slow = slow.next

    slow.next = slow.next.next                 # slow sits just before the target
    return dummy.next

    ListNode fast = dummy, slow = dummy;

        fast = fast.next;                      // open a gap of n nodes

    while (fast.next != null) {                // move both until fast is the tail
        fast = fast.next;
        slow = slow.next;
    }

    slow.next = slow.next.next;                // slow sits just before the target
    return dummy.next;
}

    let dummy = { Val = 0; Next = head }        // lets us delete the real head too
    let mutable fast = dummy
    let mutable slow = dummy

    for _ in 1 .. n do
        fast <- fast.Next.Value                 // open a gap of n nodes

    while fast.Next.IsSome do                   // move both until fast is the tail
        fast <- fast.Next.Value
        slow <- slow.Next.Value

    slow.Next <- slow.Next.Value.Next           // slow sits just before the target
    dummy.Next

{

    ListNode* fast = &dummy;
    ListNode* slow = &dummy;

    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        fast = fast->next;                         // open a gap of n nodes

    while (fast->next)                             // move both until fast is the tail

func removeNthFromEnd(head *ListNode, n int) *ListNode {
	dummy := &ListNode{Next: head} // lets us delete the real head too
	fast, slow := dummy, dummy

	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		fast = fast.Next // open a gap of n nodes
	}

	for fast.Next != nil { // move both until fast is the tail
		fast = fast.Next
		slow = slow.Next
	}

	slow.Next = slow.Next.Next // slow sits just before the target
	return dummy.Next

pub fn remove_nth_from_end(head: ListLink, n: i32) -> ListLink {
    // Safe Rust allows one mutable cursor into a Box list, so the gap of n nodes
    // becomes a position: the target sits len - n links after the dummy.
    let mut len = 0;
    let mut cur = &head;
    while let Some(node) = cur {
        len += 1;
        cur = &node.next;
    }

    let mut dummy = Box::new(ListNode { val: 0, next: head });   // lets us delete the real head too
    let mut link = &mut dummy.next;

    for _ in 0..len - n as usize {               // stop just before the target
        link = &mut link.as_mut().unwrap().next;
    }

    *link = link.take().unwrap().next;           // unlink the target
    dummy.next
}

LRU Cache#146Medium

A fixed-size cache that evicts the least recently used key, with O(1) Get and Put. A hash map finds the node; a doubly linked list keeps the order.

class DNode {
  prev: DNode = this;  // linked to itself until it's inserted
  next: DNode = this;
  constructor(public key: number, public val: number) {}
}

class LRUCache {
  private nodes = new Map<number, DNode>();
  private head = new DNode(0, 0);  // dummy before the newest
  private tail = new DNode(0, 0);  // dummy after the oldest

  constructor(private capacity: number) {
    this.head.next = this.tail;
    this.tail.prev = this.head;
  }

  get(key: number): number {
    const node = this.nodes.get(key);
    if (!node) return -1;
    this.unlink(node);
    this.addFront(node);  // just used: now the newest
    return node.val;
  }

  put(key: number, value: number): void {
    const old = this.nodes.get(key);
    if (old) this.unlink(old);
    else if (this.nodes.size === this.capacity) {
      const lru = this.tail.prev;  // the least recently used
      this.unlink(lru);
      this.nodes.delete(lru.key);
    }
    const node = new DNode(key, value);
    this.nodes.set(key, node);
    this.addFront(node);
  }

  private unlink(node: DNode): void {
    node.prev.next = node.next;
    node.next.prev = node.prev;
  }

  private addFront(node: DNode): void {
    node.prev = this.head;
    node.next = this.head.next;
    this.head.next.prev = node;
    this.head.next = node;
  }
}
class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        self.capacity = capacity
        # newest at the end, oldest at the front: an OrderedDict keeps that order
        self.order: OrderedDict[int, int] = OrderedDict()

    def get(self, key: int) -> int:
        if key not in self.order:
            return -1

        self.order.move_to_end(key)            # O(1): the dict already links the entries
        return self.order[key]

    def put(self, key: int, value: int) -> None:
        if key in self.order:
            self.order.pop(key)
        elif len(self.order) == self.capacity:
            self.order.popitem(last=False)     # evict the least recently used

        self.order[key] = value
public class LRUCache {
    private final int capacity;
    // access-order LinkedHashMap: iteration runs from least to most recently used
    private final LinkedHashMap<Integer, Integer> order;

    public LRUCache(int capacity) {
        this.capacity = capacity;
        this.order = new LinkedHashMap<>(capacity, 0.75f, true);
    }

    public int get(int key) {
        Integer value = order.get(key);        // a get also marks the key as newest
        return value == null ? -1 : value;
    }

    public void put(int key, int value) {
        order.put(key, value);
        if (order.size() > capacity)
            order.remove(order.keySet().iterator().next());   // evict the least recently used
    }
}
public class LRUCache
{
    private readonly int capacity;
    private readonly Dictionary<int, LinkedListNode<(int Key, int Val)>> nodes = new();
    private readonly LinkedList<(int Key, int Val)> order = new();   // front = newest

    public LRUCache(int capacity) => this.capacity = capacity;

    public int Get(int key)
    {
        if (!nodes.TryGetValue(key, out var node)) return -1;

        order.Remove(node);                      // O(1) because we hold the node
        order.AddFirst(node);
        return node.Value.Val;
    }

    public void Put(int key, int value)
    {
        if (nodes.TryGetValue(key, out var old))
        {
            order.Remove(old);
        }
        else if (nodes.Count == capacity)
        {
            nodes.Remove(order.Last.Value.Key);  // evict the least recently used
            order.RemoveLast();
        }

        nodes[key] = order.AddFirst((key, value));
    }
}
type LRUCache(capacity: int) =
    let nodes = Dictionary<int, LinkedListNode<int * int>>()
    let order = LinkedList<int * int>()         // front = newest

    member _.Get(key: int) =
        match nodes.TryGetValue key with
        | true, node ->
            order.Remove node |> ignore         // O(1) because we hold the node
            order.AddFirst node |> ignore
            snd node.Value
        | _ -> -1

    member _.Put(key: int, value: int) =
        match nodes.TryGetValue key with
        | true, old -> order.Remove old |> ignore
        | _ ->
            if nodes.Count = capacity then
                nodes.Remove(order.Last.Value |> fst) |> ignore   // evict the least recently used
                order.RemoveLast()

        nodes[key] <- order.AddFirst((key, value))
class LRUCache
{
    int capacity;
    list<pair<int, int>> order;                    // front = newest
    unordered_map<int, list<pair<int, int>>::iterator> nodes;

public:
    LRUCache(int cap) : capacity(cap) {}

    int get(int key)
    {
        auto it = nodes.find(key);
        if (it == nodes.end()) return -1;

        order.splice(order.begin(), order, it->second);   // O(1): we hold the iterator
        return it->second->second;
    }

    void put(int key, int value)
    {
        auto it = nodes.find(key);
        if (it != nodes.end())
        {
            it->second->second = value;
            order.splice(order.begin(), order, it->second);
            return;
        }

        if ((int)nodes.size() == capacity)
        {
            nodes.erase(order.back().first);       // evict the least recently used
            order.pop_back();
        }

        order.push_front({key, value});
        nodes[key] = order.begin();
    }
};
type lruEntry struct {
	key, val int
}

type LRUCache struct {
	capacity int
	nodes    map[int]*list.Element
	order    *list.List // front = newest
}

func newLRUCache(capacity int) LRUCache {
	return LRUCache{
		capacity: capacity,
		nodes:    make(map[int]*list.Element),
		order:    list.New(),
	}
}

func (c *LRUCache) get(key int) int {
	element, ok := c.nodes[key]
	if !ok {
		return -1
	}

	c.order.MoveToFront(element) // O(1) because we hold the element
	return element.Value.(lruEntry).val
}

func (c *LRUCache) put(key, value int) {
	if element, ok := c.nodes[key]; ok {
		c.order.Remove(element)
	} else if len(c.nodes) == c.capacity {
		oldest := c.order.Back()
		delete(c.nodes, oldest.Value.(lruEntry).key) // evict the least recently used
		c.order.Remove(oldest)
	}

	c.nodes[key] = c.order.PushFront(lruEntry{key, value})
}
struct Node {
    key: i32,
    val: i32,
    prev: usize,
    next: usize,
}

const NONE: usize = usize::MAX;

pub struct LRUCache {
    capacity: usize,
    nodes: Vec<Node>,                            // arena: slots are indexed, never moved
    index: HashMap<i32, usize>,                  // key -> slot
    free: Vec<usize>,                            // slots left behind by evictions
    head: usize,                                 // most recently used
    tail: usize,                                 // least recently used
}

impl LRUCache {
    pub fn new(capacity: i32) -> Self {
        LRUCache {
            capacity: capacity as usize,
            nodes: Vec::new(),
            index: HashMap::new(),
            free: Vec::new(),
            head: NONE,
            tail: NONE,
        }
    }

    pub fn get(&mut self, key: i32) -> i32 {
        let Some(&slot) = self.index.get(&key) else { return -1 };

        self.unlink(slot);                       // O(1) because we hold the slot
        self.push_front(slot);
        self.nodes[slot].val
    }

    pub fn put(&mut self, key: i32, value: i32) {
        if let Some(&slot) = self.index.get(&key) {
            self.unlink(slot);
            self.nodes[slot].val = value;
            self.push_front(slot);
            return;
        }

        if self.index.len() == self.capacity {
            let victim = self.tail;              // evict the least recently used
            self.unlink(victim);
            self.index.remove(&self.nodes[victim].key);
            self.free.push(victim);
        }

        let node = Node { key, val: value, prev: NONE, next: NONE };
        let slot = match self.free.pop() {
            Some(slot) => {
                self.nodes[slot] = node;         // reuse the slot an eviction freed
                slot
            }
            None => {
                self.nodes.push(node);
                self.nodes.len() - 1
            }
        };

        self.index.insert(key, slot);
        self.push_front(slot);
    }

    fn unlink(&mut self, slot: usize) {
        let (prev, next) = (self.nodes[slot].prev, self.nodes[slot].next);

        if prev == NONE { self.head = next; } else { self.nodes[prev].next = next; }
        if next == NONE { self.tail = prev; } else { self.nodes[next].prev = prev; }
    }

    fn push_front(&mut self, slot: usize) {
        self.nodes[slot].prev = NONE;
        self.nodes[slot].next = self.head;

        if self.head == NONE { self.tail = slot; } else { self.nodes[self.head].prev = slot; }
        self.head = slot;
    }
}

Time O(1) per operation · Space O(capacity)

08

Trees: DFS and BFS

Trees & graphs

Use it when the input is a TreeNode. "Level", "row", "right side view" or "closest to the root" point to BFS; heights, paths, validity and ancestors point to DFS.

How it works

  • DFS bottom-up: a call returns something about its subtree (height, sum, a found node) and the parent combines both answers.
  • DFS top-down: pass limits or the path so far down as parameters.
  • BFS: a queue. Process the nodes queued at the start of each round to handle exactly one level.
  • In a BST, an inorder traversal visits the values in sorted order.

Watch out

  • Decide first which way information flows: up (return values) or down (parameters).
  • Use limits wider than any node value, or nullable bounds, so a value equal to the smallest or largest int can't break a BST check.

DFS: Maximum Depth#104 and Validate BST#98Medium

The height of a tree (answer flows up), and whether it's a valid BST (limits flow down).

// Bottom-up: each call returns an answer about its own subtree.
function maxDepth(root: TreeNode | null): number {
  if (root === null) return 0;
  return 1 + Math.max(maxDepth(root.left), maxDepth(root.right));
}

// Top-down: pass the limits every node below must respect.
function isValidBST(root: TreeNode | null): boolean {
  return fits(root, -Infinity, Infinity);
}

function fits(node: TreeNode | null, low: number, high: number): boolean {
  if (node === null) return true;
  if (node.val <= low || node.val >= high) return false;

  return fits(node.left, low, node.val)   // left: smaller than me
    && fits(node.right, node.val, high);  // right: bigger than me
}
# Bottom-up: each call returns an answer about its own subtree.
def max_depth(root: TreeNode | None) -> int:
    if root is None:
        return 0
    return 1 + max(max_depth(root.left), max_depth(root.right))


# Top-down: pass the limits that every node below must respect.
def is_valid_bst(root: TreeNode | None) -> bool:
    return is_bst_between(root, float("-inf"), float("inf"))


def is_bst_between(node: TreeNode | None, low: float, high: float) -> bool:
    if node is None:
        return True
    if node.val <= low or node.val >= high:
        return False

    left_ok = is_bst_between(node.left, low, node.val)  # left side: smaller than me
    right_ok = is_bst_between(node.right, node.val, high)  # right side: bigger than me
    return left_ok and right_ok
// Bottom-up: each call returns an answer about its own subtree.

    return isValid(node.left, low, node.val)     // left side: smaller than me
        && isValid(node.right, node.val, high);  // right side: bigger than me

{

// Bottom-up: each call returns an answer about its own subtree.
let rec maxDepth (root: TreeNode option) : int =
    match root with
    | None -> 0
    | Some node -> 1 + max (maxDepth node.Left) (maxDepth node.Right)

// Top-down: pass the limits that every node below must respect.
let isValidBst (root: TreeNode option) : bool =
    let rec isValid (node: TreeNode option) (low: int64) (high: int64) =
        match node with
        | None -> true
        | Some n ->
            let v = int64 n.Val
            v > low && v < high
            && isValid n.Left low v                     // left side: smaller than me
            && isValid n.Right v high                   // right side: bigger than me

    isValid root Int64.MinValue Int64.MaxValue

{

}

{

        && isValid(node->right, node->val, high);  // right side: bigger than me

// Top-down: pass the limits that every node below must respect.

	return isValidRange(root, math.MinInt64, math.MaxInt64)
}

func isValidRange(node *TreeNode, low, high int64) bool {
	if node == nil {
		return true
	}
	if int64(node.Val) <= low || int64(node.Val) >= high {
		return false
	}

	return isValidRange(node.Left, low, int64(node.Val)) && // left side: smaller than me
		isValidRange(node.Right, int64(node.Val), high) // right side: bigger than me
}
// Bottom-up: each call returns an answer about its own subtree.
pub fn max_depth(root: TreeLink) -> i32 {
    let Some(node) = root else { return 0 };
    let node = node.borrow();
    1 + max_depth(node.left.clone()).max(max_depth(node.right.clone()))
}

// Top-down: pass the limits that every node below must respect.
pub fn is_valid_bst(root: TreeLink) -> bool {
    is_valid(root, i64::MIN, i64::MAX)
}

fn is_valid(node: TreeLink, low: i64, high: i64) -> bool {
    let Some(node) = node else { return true };
    let node = node.borrow();
    if i64::from(node.val) <= low || i64::from(node.val) >= high { return false; }

    let val = i64::from(node.val);
    is_valid(node.left.clone(), low, val)            // left side: smaller than me
        && is_valid(node.right.clone(), val, high)   // right side: bigger than me
}

Time O(n) · Space O(h), the height of the tree

Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree#236Medium

The lowest node with both p and q below it (a node counts as below itself).

function lowestCommonAncestor(
  root: TreeNode | null,
  p: TreeNode | null,
  q: TreeNode | null,
): TreeNode | null {
  if (root === null || root === p || root === q) return root;

  const left = lowestCommonAncestor(root.left, p, q);
  const right = lowestCommonAncestor(root.right, p, q);

  if (left !== null && right !== null) return root;  // split here
  return left ?? right;                              // pass up what's found
}
def lowest_common_ancestor(
    root: TreeNode | None, p: TreeNode, q: TreeNode
) -> TreeNode | None:
    if root is None or root is p or root is q:
        return root

    left = lowest_common_ancestor(root.left, p, q)
    right = lowest_common_ancestor(root.right, p, q)

    if left and right:
        return root                            # one on each side: split here
    return left or right                       # pass up whatever was found
public TreeNode lowestCommonAncestor(TreeNode root, TreeNode p, TreeNode q) {
    if (root == null || root == p || root == q) return root;

    TreeNode left = lowestCommonAncestor(root.left, p, q);
    TreeNode right = lowestCommonAncestor(root.right, p, q);

    if (left != null && right != null) return root;   // one on each side: split here
    return left != null ? left : right;               // pass up whatever was found
}
public TreeNode LowestCommonAncestor(TreeNode root, TreeNode p, TreeNode q)
{
    if (root == null || root == p || root == q) return root;

    TreeNode left = LowestCommonAncestor(root.left, p, q);
    TreeNode right = LowestCommonAncestor(root.right, p, q);

    if (left != null && right != null) return root;   // one on each side: split here
    return left ?? right;                             // pass up whatever was found
}
let rec lowestCommonAncestor (root: TreeNode option) (p: TreeNode) (q: TreeNode) : TreeNode option =
    match root with
    | None -> None
    | Some node ->
        if Object.ReferenceEquals(node, p) || Object.ReferenceEquals(node, q) then root
        else
            let left = lowestCommonAncestor node.Left p q
            let right = lowestCommonAncestor node.Right p q

            if left.IsSome && right.IsSome then root   // one on each side: split here
            elif left.IsSome then left                 // pass up whatever was found
            else right
TreeNode* lowestCommonAncestor(TreeNode* root, TreeNode* p, TreeNode* q)
{
    if (!root || root == p || root == q) return root;

    TreeNode* left = lowestCommonAncestor(root->left, p, q);
    TreeNode* right = lowestCommonAncestor(root->right, p, q);

    if (left && right) return root;                // one on each side: split here
    return left ? left : right;                    // pass up whatever was found
}
func lowestCommonAncestor(root, p, q *TreeNode) *TreeNode {
	if root == nil || root == p || root == q {
		return root
	}

	left := lowestCommonAncestor(root.Left, p, q)
	right := lowestCommonAncestor(root.Right, p, q)

	if left != nil && right != nil {
		return root // one on each side: split here
	}
	if left != nil {
		return left
	}
	return right // pass up whatever was found
}
pub fn lowest_common_ancestor(root: TreeLink, p: TreeLink, q: TreeLink) -> TreeLink {
    let Some(node) = root else { return None };

    let is_target = |target: &TreeLink| target.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| Rc::ptr_eq(&node, t));
    if is_target(&p) || is_target(&q) { return Some(node); }

    let (left, right) = {
        let links = node.borrow();
        (
            lowest_common_ancestor(links.left.clone(), p.clone(), q.clone()),
            lowest_common_ancestor(links.right.clone(), p.clone(), q.clone()),
        )
    };

    if left.is_some() && right.is_some() { return Some(node); }   // one on each side: split here
    left.or(right)                                                // pass up whatever was found
}

Time O(n) · Space O(h)

BFS: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal#102Medium

The values level by level, top to bottom.

function levelOrder(root: TreeNode | null): number[][] {
  const levels: number[][] = [];
  let level: TreeNode[] = root === null ? [] : [root];

  while (level.length > 0) {
    levels.push(level.map((node) => node.val));

    const next: TreeNode[] = [];  // the level below, in order
    for (const node of level) {
      if (node.left !== null) next.push(node.left);
      if (node.right !== null) next.push(node.right);
    }
    level = next;
  }

  return levels;
}
def level_order(root: TreeNode | None) -> list[list[int]]:
    levels: list[list[int]] = []
    if root is None:
        return levels

    queue: deque[TreeNode] = deque([root])

    while queue:
        size = len(queue)                      # everything queued now is one level
        level: list[int] = []

        for _ in range(size):
            node = queue.popleft()
            level.append(node.val)
            if node.left:
                queue.append(node.left)
            if node.right:
                queue.append(node.right)

        levels.append(level)

    return levels
public List<List<Integer>> levelOrder(TreeNode root) {
    List<List<Integer>> levels = new ArrayList<>();
    if (root == null) return levels;

    Queue<TreeNode> queue = new ArrayDeque<>();
    queue.offer(root);

    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        int size = queue.size();               // everything queued now is one level
        List<Integer> level = new ArrayList<>(size);

        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
            TreeNode node = queue.poll();
            level.add(node.val);
            if (node.left != null) queue.offer(node.left);
            if (node.right != null) queue.offer(node.right);
        }

        levels.add(level);
    }

    return levels;
}
public IList<IList<int>> LevelOrder(TreeNode root)
{
    var levels = new List<IList<int>>();
    if (root == null) return levels;

    var queue = new Queue<TreeNode>();
    queue.Enqueue(root);

    while (queue.Count > 0)
    {
        int size = queue.Count;                  // everything queued now is one level
        var level = new List<int>(size);

        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++)
        {
            TreeNode node = queue.Dequeue();
            level.Add(node.val);
            if (node.left != null) queue.Enqueue(node.left);
            if (node.right != null) queue.Enqueue(node.right);
        }

        levels.Add(level);
    }

    return levels;
}
let levelOrder (root: TreeNode option) : IList<IList<int>> =
    let levels = ResizeArray<IList<int>>()

    match root with
    | None -> levels :> IList<IList<int>>
    | Some start ->
        let queue = Queue<TreeNode>()
        queue.Enqueue start

        while queue.Count > 0 do
            let size = queue.Count              // everything queued now is one level
            let level = ResizeArray<int>(size)

            for _ in 1 .. size do
                let node = queue.Dequeue()
                level.Add node.Val
                if node.Left.IsSome then queue.Enqueue node.Left.Value
                if node.Right.IsSome then queue.Enqueue node.Right.Value

            levels.Add(level :> IList<int>)

        levels :> IList<IList<int>>
vector<vector<int>> levelOrder(TreeNode* root)
{
    vector<vector<int>> levels;
    if (!root) return levels;

    queue<TreeNode*> q;
    q.push(root);

    while (!q.empty())
    {
        int size = (int)q.size();                  // everything queued now is one level
        vector<int> level;
        level.reserve(size);

        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++)
        {
            TreeNode* node = q.front();
            q.pop();
            level.push_back(node->val);
            if (node->left) q.push(node->left);
            if (node->right) q.push(node->right);
        }

        levels.push_back(move(level));
    }

    return levels;
}
func levelOrder(root *TreeNode) [][]int {
	levels := [][]int{}
	if root == nil {
		return levels
	}

	queue := []*TreeNode{root}

	for len(queue) > 0 {
		size := len(queue) // everything queued now is one level
		level := make([]int, 0, size)

		for i := 0; i < size; i++ {
			node := queue[0]
			queue = queue[1:]
			level = append(level, node.Val)
			if node.Left != nil {
				queue = append(queue, node.Left)
			}
			if node.Right != nil {
				queue = append(queue, node.Right)
			}
		}

		levels = append(levels, level)
	}

	return levels
}
pub fn level_order(root: TreeLink) -> Vec<Vec<i32>> {
    let mut levels = Vec::new();
    let Some(root) = root else { return levels };

    let mut queue = VecDeque::new();
    queue.push_back(root);

    while !queue.is_empty() {
        let size = queue.len();                  // everything queued now is one level
        let mut level = Vec::with_capacity(size);

        for _ in 0..size {
            let node = queue.pop_front().unwrap();
            let node = node.borrow();
            level.push(node.val);
            if let Some(left) = node.left.clone() { queue.push_back(left); }
            if let Some(right) = node.right.clone() { queue.push_back(right); }
        }

        levels.push(level);
    }

    levels
}

Time O(n) · Space O(n)
