09

Heap / top K

Data structures

Use it when you want the k largest, smallest, closest or most frequent, "the kth" anything, to merge k sorted lists, to keep taking the min or max, or a running median.

How it works

  • For the k largest, keep a min-heap of size k: push each item, and pop when it grows past k.
  • That's O(n log k), which beats sorting when k is small.
  • Two heaps, a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half, give a running median.

Watch out

  • A priority queue pops the smallest priority. For a max-heap, reverse the comparer.
  • It can't change a priority in place: push a new entry and skip stale ones when they come out.

Kth Largest Element in an Array#215Medium

The kth largest element, without sorting everything.

// A binary heap, stored in an array. The children of slot i are
// 2i + 1 and 2i + 2, so the parent of slot i is (i - 1) / 2, rounded down.
class Heap<T> {
  private items: T[] = [];

  // compare works like sort's: (a, b) => a - b makes a min-heap.
  constructor(private compare: (a: T, b: T) => number) {}

  get size(): number {
    return this.items.length;
  }

  peek(): T | undefined {
    return this.items[0];
  }

  push(item: T): void {
    const a = this.items;
    a.push(item);    // add it at the end
    let i = a.length - 1;
    while (i > 0) {  // sift up while it beats its parent
      const parent = Math.floor((i - 1) / 2);
      if (this.compare(a[i], a[parent]) >= 0) break;
      [a[i], a[parent]] = [a[parent], a[i]];
      i = parent;
    }
  }

  pop(): T | undefined {
    const a = this.items;
    if (a.length <= 1) return a.pop();
    const top = a[0];
    a[0] = a.pop()!;  // move the last item to the top
    let i = 0;
    while (true) {    // sift down toward the better child
      let best = i;
      for (const kid of [2 * i + 1, 2 * i + 2])
        if (kid < a.length && this.compare(a[kid], a[best]) < 0) best = kid;
      if (best === i) return top;
      [a[i], a[best]] = [a[best], a[i]];
      i = best;
    }
  }
}

function findKthLargest(nums: number[], k: number): number {
  const heap = new Heap<number>((a, b) => a - b);  // a min-heap

  for (const num of nums) {
    heap.push(num);
    if (heap.size > k) heap.pop();  // drop the smallest of k + 1
  }

  return heap.peek()!;  // the smallest of the k largest
}
def find_kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    heap: list[int] = []                       # min-heap: smallest on top

    for num in nums:
        heapq.heappush(heap, num)
        if len(heap) > k:
            heapq.heappop(heap)                # drop the smallest, keep the k largest

    return heap[0]                             # smallest of the k largest
public int findKthLargest(int[] nums, int k) {
    PriorityQueue<Integer> heap = new PriorityQueue<>();   // min-heap: smallest on top

    for (int num : nums) {
        heap.offer(num);
        if (heap.size() > k) heap.poll();      // drop the smallest, keep the k largest
    }

    return heap.peek();                        // smallest of the k largest
}
public int FindKthLargest(int[] nums, int k)
{
    var heap = new PriorityQueue<int, int>();    // min-heap: smallest on top

    foreach (int num in nums)
    {
        heap.Enqueue(num, num);
        if (heap.Count > k) heap.Dequeue();      // drop the smallest, keep the k largest
    }

    return heap.Peek();                          // smallest of the k largest
}
let findKthLargest (nums: int[]) (k: int) : int =
    let heap = PriorityQueue<int, int>()        // min-heap: smallest on top

    for num in nums do
        heap.Enqueue(num, num)
        if heap.Count > k then heap.Dequeue() |> ignore   // drop the smallest, keep the k largest

    heap.Peek()                                 // smallest of the k largest
int findKthLargest(vector<int>& nums, int k)
{
    priority_queue<int, vector<int>, greater<int>> heap;   // min-heap: smallest on top

    for (int num : nums)
    {
        heap.push(num);
        if ((int)heap.size() > k) heap.pop();      // drop the smallest, keep the k largest
    }

    return heap.top();                             // smallest of the k largest
}
// intMinHeap is a min-heap of ints: the five methods container/heap asks for.
type intMinHeap []int

func (h intMinHeap) Len() int           { return len(h) }
func (h intMinHeap) Less(i, j int) bool { return h[i] < h[j] }
func (h intMinHeap) Swap(i, j int)      { h[i], h[j] = h[j], h[i] }
func (h *intMinHeap) Push(x any)        { *h = append(*h, x.(int)) }

func (h *intMinHeap) Pop() any {
	old := *h
	n := len(old)
	x := old[n-1]
	*h = old[:n-1]
	return x
}

func findKthLargest(nums []int, k int) int {
	h := &intMinHeap{} // min-heap: smallest on top
	heap.Init(h)

	for _, num := range nums {
		heap.Push(h, num)
		if h.Len() > k {
			heap.Pop(h) // drop the smallest, keep the k largest
		}
	}

	return (*h)[0] // smallest of the k largest
}
pub fn find_kth_largest(nums: &[i32], k: usize) -> i32 {
    let mut heap = BinaryHeap::new();            // BinaryHeap<Reverse<i32>>: smallest on top

    for &num in nums {
        heap.push(Reverse(num));
        if heap.len() > k { heap.pop(); }        // drop the smallest, keep the k largest
    }

    heap.peek().unwrap().0                       // smallest of the k largest
}

Time O(n log k) · Space O(k)

Top K Frequent Elements#347Medium

The k most frequent numbers. A hash map counts; the heap ranks by count.

// A binary heap, stored in an array. The children of slot i are
// 2i + 1 and 2i + 2, so the parent of slot i is (i - 1) / 2, rounded down.
class Heap<T> {
  private items: T[] = [];

  // compare works like sort's: (a, b) => a - b makes a min-heap.
  constructor(private compare: (a: T, b: T) => number) {}

  get size(): number {
    return this.items.length;
  }

  peek(): T | undefined {
    return this.items[0];
  }

  push(item: T): void {
    const a = this.items;
    a.push(item);    // add it at the end
    let i = a.length - 1;
    while (i > 0) {  // sift up while it beats its parent
      const parent = Math.floor((i - 1) / 2);
      if (this.compare(a[i], a[parent]) >= 0) break;
      [a[i], a[parent]] = [a[parent], a[i]];
      i = parent;
    }
  }

  pop(): T | undefined {
    const a = this.items;
    if (a.length <= 1) return a.pop();
    const top = a[0];
    a[0] = a.pop()!;  // move the last item to the top
    let i = 0;
    while (true) {    // sift down toward the better child
      let best = i;
      for (const kid of [2 * i + 1, 2 * i + 2])
        if (kid < a.length && this.compare(a[kid], a[best]) < 0) best = kid;
      if (best === i) return top;
      [a[i], a[best]] = [a[best], a[i]];
      i = best;
    }
  }
}

function topKFrequent(nums: number[], k: number): number[] {
  const counts = new Map<number, number>();
  for (const num of nums)
    counts.set(num, (counts.get(num) ?? 0) + 1);

  // [number, count] pairs, the least frequent on top
  const heap = new Heap<[number, number]>((a, b) => a[1] - b[1]);
  for (const entry of counts) {
    heap.push(entry);
    if (heap.size > k) heap.pop();  // evict the least frequent
  }

  const result: number[] = [];
  while (heap.size > 0) result.push(heap.pop()![0]);
  return result.reverse();  // the most frequent first
}
def top_k_frequent(nums: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    counts: dict[int, int] = {}
    for num in nums:
        counts[num] = counts.get(num, 0) + 1

    heap: list[tuple[int, int]] = []           # (priority, element): priority is the count
    for num, count in counts.items():
        heapq.heappush(heap, (count, num))
        if len(heap) > k:
            heapq.heappop(heap)                # evict the least frequent

    result = [0] * k
    for i in range(k - 1, -1, -1):
        result[i] = heapq.heappop(heap)[1]     # most frequent ends up first
    return result
public int[] topKFrequent(int[] nums, int k) {
    Map<Integer, Integer> counts = new HashMap<>();
    for (int num : nums)
        counts.put(num, counts.getOrDefault(num, 0) + 1);

    // element: number, priority: count
    PriorityQueue<int[]> heap = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> a[1] - b[1]);
    for (Map.Entry<Integer, Integer> entry : counts.entrySet()) {
        heap.offer(new int[] {entry.getKey(), entry.getValue()});
        if (heap.size() > k) heap.poll();      // evict the least frequent
    }

    int[] result = new int[k];
    for (int i = k - 1; i >= 0; i--)
        result[i] = heap.poll()[0];            // most frequent ends up first
    return result;
}
public int[] TopKFrequent(int[] nums, int k)
{
    var counts = new Dictionary<int, int>();
    foreach (int num in nums)
        counts[num] = counts.GetValueOrDefault(num) + 1;

    var heap = new PriorityQueue<int, int>();    // element: number, priority: count
    foreach (var (num, count) in counts)
    {
        heap.Enqueue(num, count);
        if (heap.Count > k) heap.Dequeue();      // evict the least frequent
    }

    var result = new int[k];
    for (int i = k - 1; i >= 0; i--)
        result[i] = heap.Dequeue();              // most frequent ends up first
    return result;
}
let topKFrequent (nums: int[]) (k: int) : int[] =
    let counts = Dictionary<int, int>()
    for num in nums do
        counts[num] <- (match counts.TryGetValue num with | true, c -> c | _ -> 0) + 1

    let heap = PriorityQueue<int, int>()        // element: number, priority: count
    for pair in counts do
        heap.Enqueue(pair.Key, pair.Value)
        if heap.Count > k then heap.Dequeue() |> ignore   // evict the least frequent

    let result = Array.zeroCreate<int> k
    for i in k - 1 .. -1 .. 0 do
        result[i] <- heap.Dequeue()             // most frequent ends up first
    result
vector<int> topKFrequent(vector<int>& nums, int k)
{
    unordered_map<int, int> counts;
    for (int num : nums)
        counts[num]++;

    // (priority, element) = (count, number): greater<> keeps the least frequent on top
    priority_queue<pair<int, int>, vector<pair<int, int>>, greater<>> heap;
    for (auto& [num, count] : counts)
    {
        heap.push({count, num});
        if ((int)heap.size() > k) heap.pop();      // evict the least frequent
    }

    vector<int> result(k);
    for (int i = k - 1; i >= 0; i--)
    {
        result[i] = heap.top().second;             // most frequent ends up first
        heap.pop();
    }
    return result;
}
type freqItem struct {
	num, count int
}

// freqHeap keeps the least frequent item on top.
type freqHeap []freqItem

func (h freqHeap) Len() int           { return len(h) }
func (h freqHeap) Less(i, j int) bool { return h[i].count < h[j].count }
func (h freqHeap) Swap(i, j int)      { h[i], h[j] = h[j], h[i] }
func (h *freqHeap) Push(x any)        { *h = append(*h, x.(freqItem)) }

func (h *freqHeap) Pop() any {
	old := *h
	n := len(old)
	x := old[n-1]
	*h = old[:n-1]
	return x
}

func topKFrequent(nums []int, k int) []int {
	counts := map[int]int{}
	for _, num := range nums {
		counts[num]++
	}

	h := &freqHeap{} // element: number, priority: count
	heap.Init(h)
	for num, count := range counts {
		heap.Push(h, freqItem{num, count})
		if h.Len() > k {
			heap.Pop(h) // evict the least frequent
		}
	}

	result := make([]int, k)
	for i := k - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		result[i] = heap.Pop(h).(freqItem).num // most frequent ends up first
	}
	return result
}
pub fn top_k_frequent(nums: &[i32], k: usize) -> Vec<i32> {
    let mut counts = HashMap::new();
    for &num in nums {
        *counts.entry(num).or_insert(0) += 1;
    }

    // Element: number, priority: count. Tuple order compares the count first.
    let mut heap: BinaryHeap<Reverse<(i32, i32)>> = BinaryHeap::new();
    for (&num, &count) in &counts {
        heap.push(Reverse((count, num)));
        if heap.len() > k { heap.pop(); }        // evict the least frequent
    }

    let mut result = vec![0; k];
    for i in (0..k).rev() {
        let Reverse((_, num)) = heap.pop().unwrap();
        result[i] = num;                         // most frequent ends up first
    }
    result
}

Time O(n log k) · Space O(n)

10

Graph BFS / DFS

Trees & graphs

Use it when you see a grid of cells, islands or regions, connected components, "the minimum number of steps", something spreading over time, or explicit edges and adjacency lists.

How it works

  • DFS (recursion) floods one whole component. BFS (a queue) finds the fewest steps.
  • Multi-source BFS: enqueue every starting point first, then each level is one unit of time.
  • For explicit edges, build an adjacency list (List<int>[]) before you search.

Watch out

  • Mark a cell visited when you enqueue it. Marking on dequeue lets it enter the queue many times.
  • Deep recursion on a huge grid can overflow the stack; switch to BFS or an explicit stack.

Number of Islands#200Medium

Count the groups of connected '1' cells in a grid.

function numIslands(grid: string[][]): number {
  let islands = 0;

  for (let r = 0; r < grid.length; r++) {
    for (let c = 0; c < grid[0].length; c++) {
      if (grid[r][c] !== "1") continue;
      islands++;
      sink(grid, r, c);  // erase it so it counts once
    }
  }

  return islands;
}

function sink(grid: string[][], r: number, c: number): void {
  if (r < 0 || c < 0 || r >= grid.length || c >= grid[0].length) return;
  if (grid[r][c] !== "1") return;

  grid[r][c] = "0";  // mark it visited
  sink(grid, r + 1, c);
  sink(grid, r - 1, c);
  sink(grid, r, c + 1);
  sink(grid, r, c - 1);
}
def num_islands(grid: list[list[str]]) -> int:
    islands = 0

    for r in range(len(grid)):
        for c in range(len(grid[0])):
            if grid[r][c] != "1":
                continue
            islands += 1
            sink(grid, r, c)                   # erase the island so it counts once

    return islands

    sink(grid, r + 1, c)
    sink(grid, r - 1, c)
    sink(grid, r, c + 1)
    sink(grid, r, c - 1)

}

private static void Sink(char[][] grid, int r, int c)
{
    if (r < 0 || c < 0 || r >= grid.Length || c >= grid[0].Length) return;
    if (grid[r][c] != '1') return;

    grid[r][c] = '0';                            // mark visited

let numIslands (grid: char[][]) : int =
    let rows = grid.Length
    let cols = grid[0].Length

    let rec sink r c =
        if r >= 0 && c >= 0 && r < rows && c < cols && grid[r][c] = '1' then
            grid[r][c] <- '0'                   // mark visited
            sink (r + 1) c
            sink (r - 1) c
            sink r (c + 1)
            sink r (c - 1)

    let mutable islands = 0

        for c in 0 .. cols - 1 do

                islands <- islands + 1
                sink r c                        // erase the island so it counts once

    islands

func sink(grid [][]byte, r, c int) {
	if r < 0 || c < 0 || r >= len(grid) || c >= len(grid[0]) {
		return
	}
	if grid[r][c] != '1' {

	grid[r][c] = '0' // mark visited

pub fn num_islands(grid: &mut [Vec<char>]) -> i32 {
    let mut islands = 0;

    for r in 0..grid.len() {
        for c in 0..grid[0].len() {
            if grid[r][c] != '1' { continue; }
            islands += 1;
            sink(grid, r, c);                    // erase the island so it counts once
        }
    }

    islands
}

fn sink(grid: &mut [Vec<char>], r: usize, c: usize) {
    if grid[r][c] != '1' { return; }

    grid[r][c] = '0';                            // mark visited
    if r + 1 < grid.len() { sink(grid, r + 1, c); }
    if r > 0 { sink(grid, r - 1, c); }
    if c + 1 < grid[0].len() { sink(grid, r, c + 1); }
    if c > 0 { sink(grid, r, c - 1); }
}

Time O(rows · cols) · Space O(rows · cols) for the recursion in the worst case

Rotting Oranges#994Medium

Each minute, rotten oranges rot their fresh neighbors. How many minutes until none are fresh (or -1)?

function orangesRotting(grid: number[][]): number {
  const rows = grid.length, cols = grid[0].length;
  let rotten: [number, number][] = [];
  let fresh = 0;

  for (let r = 0; r < rows; r++)
    for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
      if (grid[r][c] === 2) rotten.push([r, c]);  // every source at once
      else if (grid[r][c] === 1) fresh++;
    }

  const steps = [[1, 0], [-1, 0], [0, 1], [0, -1]];
  let minutes = 0;

  while (rotten.length > 0 && fresh > 0) {
    const next: [number, number][] = [];  // rots during this minute
    for (const [r, c] of rotten)
      for (const [dr, dc] of steps) {
        const nr = r + dr, nc = c + dc;
        if (nr < 0 || nc < 0 || nr >= rows || nc >= cols) continue;
        if (grid[nr][nc] !== 1) continue;

        grid[nr][nc] = 2;  // mark it as you collect it
        fresh--;
        next.push([nr, nc]);
      }
    rotten = next;
    minutes++;
  }

  return fresh === 0 ? minutes : -1;
}
def oranges_rotting(grid: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    fresh = 0
    queue: deque[tuple[int, int]] = deque()

    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            if grid[r][c] == 2:
                queue.append((r, c))           # every source starts at once
            elif grid[r][c] == 1:
                fresh += 1

    steps = ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1))
    minutes = 0

    while queue and fresh > 0:
        for _ in range(len(queue)):            # one level = one minute
            r, c = queue.popleft()
            for dr, dc in steps:
                nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
                if nr < 0 or nc < 0 or nr >= rows or nc >= cols:
                    continue
                if grid[nr][nc] != 1:
                    continue

                grid[nr][nc] = 2               # mark when queued
                fresh -= 1
                queue.append((nr, nc))
        minutes += 1

    return minutes if fresh == 0 else -1
public int orangesRotting(int[][] grid) {
    int rows = grid.length, cols = grid[0].length;
    int fresh = 0;
    Queue<int[]> queue = new ArrayDeque<>();

    for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
            if (grid[r][c] == 2) queue.offer(new int[] {r, c});   // every source starts at once
            else if (grid[r][c] == 1) fresh++;
        }
    }

    int[][] steps = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}};
    int minutes = 0;

    while (!queue.isEmpty() && fresh > 0) {
        for (int i = queue.size(); i > 0; i--) {     // one level = one minute
            int[] cell = queue.poll();
            int r = cell[0], c = cell[1];

            for (int[] step : steps) {
                int nr = r + step[0], nc = c + step[1];
                if (nr < 0 || nc < 0 || nr >= rows || nc >= cols) continue;
                if (grid[nr][nc] != 1) continue;

                grid[nr][nc] = 2;                // mark when queued
                fresh--;
                queue.offer(new int[] {nr, nc});
            }
        }
        minutes++;
    }

    return fresh == 0 ? minutes : -1;
}

            else if (grid[r][c] == 1) fresh++;
        }
    }

    var steps = new[] { (1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1) };
    int minutes = 0;

    while (queue.Count > 0 && fresh > 0)
    {
        for (int i = queue.Count; i > 0; i--)            // one level = one minute
        {
            var (r, c) = queue.Dequeue();
            foreach (var (dr, dc) in steps)
            {
                int nr = r + dr, nc = c + dc;
                if (nr < 0 || nc < 0 || nr >= rows || nc >= cols) continue;
                if (grid[nr][nc] != 1) continue;

                grid[nr][nc] = 2;                         // mark when queued
                fresh--;
                queue.Enqueue((nr, nc));
            }
        }
        minutes++;
    }

    return fresh == 0 ? minutes : -1;
}
let orangesRotting (grid: int[][]) : int =
    let rows = grid.Length
    let cols = grid[0].Length
    let queue = Queue<int * int>()
    let mutable fresh = 0

    for r in 0 .. rows - 1 do
        for c in 0 .. cols - 1 do
            if grid[r][c] = 2 then queue.Enqueue((r, c))   // every source starts at once
            elif grid[r][c] = 1 then fresh <- fresh + 1

    let steps = [| (1, 0); (-1, 0); (0, 1); (0, -1) |]
    let mutable minutes = 0

    while queue.Count > 0 && fresh > 0 do

        for _ in 1 .. size do
            let (r, c) = queue.Dequeue()

                let nr = r + dr
                let nc = c + dc

                    grid[nr][nc] <- 2                // mark when queued
                    fresh <- fresh - 1
                    queue.Enqueue((nr, nc))

int orangesRotting(vector<vector<int>>& grid)
{
    int rows = (int)grid.size(), cols = (int)grid[0].size(), fresh = 0;
    queue<pair<int, int>> q;

    for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++)
    {
        for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++)
        {
            if (grid[r][c] == 2) q.push({r, c});   // every source starts at once
            else if (grid[r][c] == 1) fresh++;
        }
    }

    const int steps[4][2] = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}};
    int minutes = 0;

    while (!q.empty() && fresh > 0)
    {
        for (int i = (int)q.size(); i > 0; i--)    // one level = one minute
        {
            auto [r, c] = q.front();
            q.pop();
            for (auto& step : steps)
            {
                int nr = r + step[0], nc = c + step[1];
                if (nr < 0 || nc < 0 || nr >= rows || nc >= cols) continue;
                if (grid[nr][nc] != 1) continue;

                grid[nr][nc] = 2;                  // mark when queued
                fresh--;
                q.push({nr, nc});
            }
        }
        minutes++;
    }

    return fresh == 0 ? minutes : -1;
}
func orangesRotting(grid [][]int) int {
	rows, cols := len(grid), len(grid[0])
	fresh := 0
	queue := [][2]int{}

	for r := 0; r < rows; r++ {
		for c := 0; c < cols; c++ {
			if grid[r][c] == 2 {
				queue = append(queue, [2]int{r, c}) // every source starts at once
			} else if grid[r][c] == 1 {
				fresh++
			}
		}
	}

	steps := [][2]int{{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}}
	minutes := 0

	for len(queue) > 0 && fresh > 0 {
		for i := len(queue); i > 0; i-- { // one level = one minute
			cell := queue[0]
			queue = queue[1:]
			r, c := cell[0], cell[1]
			for _, step := range steps {
				nr, nc := r+step[0], c+step[1]
				if nr < 0 || nc < 0 || nr >= rows || nc >= cols {
					continue
				}
				if grid[nr][nc] != 1 {
					continue
				}

				grid[nr][nc] = 2 // mark when queued
				fresh--
				queue = append(queue, [2]int{nr, nc})
			}
		}
		minutes++
	}

	if fresh == 0 {
		return minutes
	}
	return -1
}
pub fn oranges_rotting(grid: &mut [Vec<i32>]) -> i32 {
    let (rows, cols) = (grid.len(), grid[0].len());
    let mut fresh = 0;
    let mut queue = VecDeque::new();

    for r in 0..rows {
        for c in 0..cols {
            if grid[r][c] == 2 { queue.push_back((r, c)); }   // every source starts at once
            else if grid[r][c] == 1 { fresh += 1; }
        }
    }

    let steps: [(isize, isize); 4] = [(1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)];
    let mut minutes = 0;

    while !queue.is_empty() && fresh > 0 {
        for _ in 0..queue.len() {                // one level = one minute
            let (r, c) = queue.pop_front().unwrap();
            for (dr, dc) in steps {
                let nr = r as isize + dr;
                let nc = c as isize + dc;
                if nr < 0 || nc < 0 || nr >= rows as isize || nc >= cols as isize { continue; }

                let (nr, nc) = (nr as usize, nc as usize);
                if grid[nr][nc] != 1 { continue; }

                grid[nr][nc] = 2;                // mark when queued
                fresh -= 1;
                queue.push_back((nr, nc));
            }
        }
        minutes += 1;
    }

    if fresh == 0 { minutes } else { -1 }
}

Time O(rows · cols) · Space O(rows · cols)

11

Topological sort

Trees & graphs

Use it when you see prerequisites, dependencies, a build or task order, "is it possible to finish?", or need to detect a cycle in a directed graph.

How it works

  • Count the incoming edges (the indegree) of every node.
  • Queue every node with indegree 0. When you take one, decrement its neighbors and queue any that reach 0.
  • If some nodes never reach 0, the graph has a cycle.

Watch out

  • Get the edge direction right: [course, prerequisite] means prerequisite -> course.
  • Course Schedule (#207) is the same code returning the order, then checking its length against the course count.

Course Schedule II#210Medium

Return an order that takes every course, or an empty array if that's impossible.

function findOrder(
  numCourses: number,
  prerequisites: number[][],
): number[] {
  // Array.from gives each course its own list; fill([]) would share one.
  const unlocks: number[][] = Array.from({ length: numCourses }, () => []);
  const indegree: number[] = new Array(numCourses).fill(0);

  for (const [course, pre] of prerequisites) {
    unlocks[pre].push(course);  // edge: prerequisite -> course
    indegree[course]++;
  }

  const order: number[] = [];
  for (let c = 0; c < numCourses; c++)
    if (indegree[c] === 0) order.push(c);  // nothing blocks these

  // order doubles as the queue: head walks it, freed courses join the end
  for (let head = 0; head < order.length; head++)
    for (const next of unlocks[order[head]])
      if (--indegree[next] === 0) order.push(next);

  return order.length === numCourses ? order : [];  // short: a cycle
}
def find_order(num_courses: int, prerequisites: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
    unlocks: list[list[int]] = [[] for _ in range(num_courses)]
    indegree = [0] * num_courses

    for course, prereq in prerequisites:       # p = [course, prerequisite]
        unlocks[prereq].append(course)         # edge: prerequisite -> course
        indegree[course] += 1

    ready: deque[int] = deque()
    for i in range(num_courses):
        if indegree[i] == 0:
            ready.append(i)                    # nothing blocks these

    order: list[int] = []
    while ready:
        course = ready.popleft()
        order.append(course)

        for nxt in unlocks[course]:
            indegree[nxt] -= 1
            if indegree[nxt] == 0:
                ready.append(nxt)

    return order if len(order) == num_courses else []  # leftovers = cycle
public int[] findOrder(int numCourses, int[][] prerequisites) {
    List<List<Integer>> unlocks = new ArrayList<>(numCourses);
    int[] indegree = new int[numCourses];
    for (int i = 0; i < numCourses; i++) unlocks.add(new ArrayList<>());

    for (int[] p : prerequisites) {            // p = [course, prerequisite]
        unlocks.get(p[1]).add(p[0]);            // edge: prerequisite -> course
        indegree[p[0]]++;
    }

    Queue<Integer> ready = new ArrayDeque<>();
    for (int i = 0; i < numCourses; i++)
        if (indegree[i] == 0) ready.offer(i);   // nothing blocks these

    List<Integer> order = new ArrayList<>();
    while (!ready.isEmpty()) {
        int course = ready.poll();
        order.add(course);

        for (int next : unlocks.get(course))
            if (--indegree[next] == 0) ready.offer(next);
    }

    int[] taken = order.stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).toArray();
    return order.size() == numCourses ? taken : new int[0];   // leftovers = cycle
}
public int[] FindOrder(int numCourses, int[][] prerequisites)
{
    var unlocks = new List<int>[numCourses];
    var indegree = new int[numCourses];
    for (int i = 0; i < numCourses; i++) unlocks[i] = [];

    foreach (int[] p in prerequisites)           // p = [course, prerequisite]
    {
        unlocks[p[1]].Add(p[0]);                 // edge: prerequisite -> course
        indegree[p[0]]++;
    }

    var ready = new Queue<int>();
    for (int i = 0; i < numCourses; i++)
        if (indegree[i] == 0) ready.Enqueue(i);  // nothing blocks these

    var order = new List<int>();
    while (ready.Count > 0)
    {
        int course = ready.Dequeue();
        order.Add(course);

        foreach (int next in unlocks[course])
            if (--indegree[next] == 0) ready.Enqueue(next);
    }

    return order.Count == numCourses ? order.ToArray() : [];   // leftovers = cycle
}
let findOrder (numCourses: int) (prerequisites: int[][]) : int[] =
    let unlocks = Array.init numCourses (fun _ -> ResizeArray<int>())
    let indegree = Array.zeroCreate<int> numCourses

    for p in prerequisites do                   // p = [course, prerequisite]
        unlocks[p[1]].Add p[0]                  // edge: prerequisite -> course
        indegree[p[0]] <- indegree[p[0]] + 1

    let ready = Queue<int>()
    for i in 0 .. numCourses - 1 do
        if indegree[i] = 0 then ready.Enqueue i   // nothing blocks these

    let order = ResizeArray<int>()
    while ready.Count > 0 do
        let course = ready.Dequeue()
        order.Add course

        for next in unlocks[course] do
            indegree[next] <- indegree[next] - 1
            if indegree[next] = 0 then ready.Enqueue next

    if order.Count = numCourses then order.ToArray() else [||]   // leftovers = cycle
vector<int> findOrder(int numCourses, vector<vector<int>>& prerequisites)
{
    vector<vector<int>> unlocks(numCourses);
    vector<int> indegree(numCourses, 0);

    for (auto& p : prerequisites)                  // p = [course, prerequisite]
    {
        unlocks[p[1]].push_back(p[0]);             // edge: prerequisite -> course
        indegree[p[0]]++;
    }

    queue<int> ready;
    for (int i = 0; i < numCourses; i++)
        if (indegree[i] == 0) ready.push(i);       // nothing blocks these

    vector<int> order;
    while (!ready.empty())
    {
        int course = ready.front();
        ready.pop();
        order.push_back(course);

        for (int next : unlocks[course])
            if (--indegree[next] == 0) ready.push(next);
    }

    // leftovers = cycle
    return (int)order.size() == numCourses ? order : vector<int>{};
}
func findOrder(numCourses int, prerequisites [][]int) []int {
	unlocks := make([][]int, numCourses)
	indegree := make([]int, numCourses)

	for _, p := range prerequisites { // p = [course, prerequisite]
		unlocks[p[1]] = append(unlocks[p[1]], p[0]) // edge: prerequisite -> course
		indegree[p[0]]++
	}

	ready := []int{}
	for i := 0; i < numCourses; i++ {
		if indegree[i] == 0 {
			ready = append(ready, i) // nothing blocks these
		}
	}

	order := []int{}
	for len(ready) > 0 {
		course := ready[0]
		ready = ready[1:]
		order = append(order, course)

		for _, next := range unlocks[course] {
			indegree[next]--
			if indegree[next] == 0 {
				ready = append(ready, next)
			}
		}
	}

	if len(order) == numCourses {
		return order
	}
	return []int{} // leftovers = cycle
}
pub fn find_order(num_courses: i32, prerequisites: &[Vec<i32>]) -> Vec<i32> {
    let n = num_courses as usize;
    let mut unlocks = vec![Vec::new(); n];
    let mut indegree = vec![0; n];

    for p in prerequisites {                     // p = [course, prerequisite]
        unlocks[p[1] as usize].push(p[0]);        // edge: prerequisite -> course
        indegree[p[0] as usize] += 1;
    }

    let mut ready = VecDeque::new();
    for i in 0..n {
        if indegree[i] == 0 { ready.push_back(i as i32); }   // nothing blocks these
    }

    let mut order = Vec::new();
    while let Some(course) = ready.pop_front() {
        order.push(course);

        for &next in &unlocks[course as usize] {
            indegree[next as usize] -= 1;
            if indegree[next as usize] == 0 { ready.push_back(next); }
        }
    }

    if order.len() == n { order } else { Vec::new() }   // leftovers = cycle
}

Time O(V + E) · Space O(V + E)

12

Backtracking

Recursion & DP

Use it when you must return all combinations, permutations, subsets, partitions or paths, solve a constraint puzzle, or n is small (around 20 or less).

How it works

  • Build a candidate one step at a time: choose, explore (recurse), undo.
  • Subsets and combinations loop from start and recurse with i + 1.
  • Permutations loop from 0 every time and track used[].
  • Prune: abandon a branch as soon as it can't succeed.

Watch out

  • Save a copy of the path ([.. path]), not the list you keep changing.
  • With duplicates in the input, sort, then skip nums[i] == nums[i - 1] when i > start.

Subsets#78Medium

Every subset of a list of distinct numbers.

function subsets(nums: number[]): number[][] {
  const result: number[][] = [];
  const path: number[] = [];

  function explore(start: number): void {
    result.push([...path]);  // every node is a subset: copy it

    for (let i = start; i < nums.length; i++) {
      path.push(nums[i]);  // choose
      explore(i + 1);      // explore, with later numbers only
      path.pop();          // undo
    }
  }

  explore(0);
  return result;
}
def subsets(nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
    result: list[list[int]] = []
    path: list[int] = []

    def explore(start: int) -> None:
        result.append(path.copy())             # every node is a subset: save a copy

        for i in range(start, len(nums)):
            path.append(nums[i])               # choose
            explore(i + 1)                     # explore, using later numbers only
            path.pop()                         # undo

    explore(0)
    return result
public List<List<Integer>> subsets(int[] nums) {
    List<List<Integer>> result = new ArrayList<>();
    exploreSubsets(nums, 0, new ArrayList<>(), result);
    return result;
}

private static void exploreSubsets(int[] nums, int start, List<Integer> path,
                                   List<List<Integer>> result) {
    result.add(new ArrayList<>(path));         // every node is a subset: save a copy

    for (int i = start; i < nums.length; i++) {
        path.add(nums[i]);                     // choose
        exploreSubsets(nums, i + 1, path, result);   // explore, using later numbers only
        path.remove(path.size() - 1);          // undo
    }
}
public IList<IList<int>> Subsets(int[] nums)
{
    var result = new List<IList<int>>();
    var path = new List<int>();

    void Explore(int start)
    {
        result.Add([.. path]);                   // every node is a subset: save a copy

        for (int i = start; i < nums.Length; i++)
        {
            path.Add(nums[i]);                   // choose
            Explore(i + 1);                      // explore, using later numbers only
            path.RemoveAt(path.Count - 1);       // undo
        }
    }

    Explore(0);
    return result;
}
let subsets (nums: int[]) : IList<IList<int>> =
    let result = ResizeArray<IList<int>>()
    let path = ResizeArray<int>()

    let rec explore start =
        result.Add(path.ToArray() :> IList<int>)   // every node is a subset: save a copy

        for i in start .. nums.Length - 1 do
            path.Add nums[i]                       // choose
            explore (i + 1)                       // explore, using later numbers only
            path.RemoveAt(path.Count - 1)         // undo

    explore 0
    result :> IList<IList<int>>
vector<vector<int>> subsets(vector<int>& nums)
{
    vector<vector<int>> result;
    vector<int> path;

    function<void(int)> explore = [&](int start)
    {
        result.push_back(path);                    // every node is a subset: save a copy

        for (int i = start; i < (int)nums.size(); i++)
        {
            path.push_back(nums[i]);               // choose
            explore(i + 1);                        // explore, using later numbers only
            path.pop_back();                       // undo
        }
    };

    explore(0);
    return result;
}
func subsets(nums []int) [][]int {
	result := [][]int{}
	path := []int{}

	var explore func(start int)
	explore = func(start int) {
		result = append(result, slices.Clone(path)) // every node is a subset: save a copy

		for i := start; i < len(nums); i++ {
			path = append(path, nums[i]) // choose
			explore(i + 1)               // explore, using later numbers only
			path = path[:len(path)-1]    // undo
		}
	}

	explore(0)
	return result
}
pub fn subsets(nums: &[i32]) -> Vec<Vec<i32>> {
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    let mut path = Vec::new();

    explore_subsets(nums, 0, &mut path, &mut result);
    result
}

fn explore_subsets(nums: &[i32], start: usize, path: &mut Vec<i32>, result: &mut Vec<Vec<i32>>) {
    result.push(path.clone());                   // every node is a subset: save a copy

    for i in start..nums.len() {
        path.push(nums[i]);                      // choose
        explore_subsets(nums, i + 1, path, result);   // explore, using later numbers only
        path.pop();                              // undo
    }
}

Time O(n · 2n) · Space O(n) besides the output

Permutations#46Medium

Every ordering of a list of distinct numbers.

function permute(nums: number[]): number[][] {
  const result: number[][] = [];
  const path: number[] = [];
  const used: boolean[] = new Array(nums.length).fill(false);

  function explore(): void {
    if (path.length === nums.length) {
      result.push([...path]);
      return;
    }

    for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {  // order matters: from 0
      if (used[i]) continue;

      used[i] = true;
      path.push(nums[i]);
      explore();
      path.pop();
      used[i] = false;
    }
  }

  explore();
  return result;
}
def permute(nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
    result: list[list[int]] = []
    path: list[int] = []
    used = [False] * len(nums)

    def explore() -> None:
        if len(path) == len(nums):
            result.append(path.copy())
            return

        for i in range(len(nums)):             # order matters: scan from 0 each time
            if used[i]:
                continue

            used[i] = True
            path.append(nums[i])
            explore()
            path.pop()
            used[i] = False

    explore()
    return result
public List<List<Integer>> permute(int[] nums) {
    List<List<Integer>> result = new ArrayList<>();
    explorePermutations(nums, new boolean[nums.length], new ArrayList<>(), result);
    return result;
}

private static void explorePermutations(int[] nums, boolean[] used, List<Integer> path,
                                        List<List<Integer>> result) {
    if (path.size() == nums.length) {
        result.add(new ArrayList<>(path));
        return;
    }

    for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {   // order matters: scan from 0 each time
        if (used[i]) continue;

        used[i] = true;
        path.add(nums[i]);
        explorePermutations(nums, used, path, result);
        path.remove(path.size() - 1);
        used[i] = false;
    }
}
public IList<IList<int>> Permute(int[] nums)
{
    var result = new List<IList<int>>();
    var path = new List<int>();
    var used = new bool[nums.Length];

    void Explore()
    {
        if (path.Count == nums.Length)
        {
            result.Add([.. path]);
            return;
        }

        for (int i = 0; i < nums.Length; i++)    // order matters: scan from 0 each time
        {
            if (used[i]) continue;

            used[i] = true;
            path.Add(nums[i]);
            Explore();
            path.RemoveAt(path.Count - 1);
            used[i] = false;
        }
    }

    Explore();
    return result;
}
let permute (nums: int[]) : IList<IList<int>> =
    let result = ResizeArray<IList<int>>()
    let path = ResizeArray<int>()
    let used = Array.create nums.Length false

    let rec explore () =
        if path.Count = nums.Length then
            result.Add(path.ToArray() :> IList<int>)
        else
            for i in 0 .. nums.Length - 1 do      // order matters: scan from 0 each time
                if not used[i] then
                    used[i] <- true
                    path.Add nums[i]
                    explore ()
                    path.RemoveAt(path.Count - 1)
                    used[i] <- false

    explore ()
    result :> IList<IList<int>>

{
    vector<vector<int>> result;
    vector<int> path;
    vector<bool> used(nums.size(), false);

    function<void()> explore = [&]()
    {
        if (path.size() == nums.size())
        {
            result.push_back(path);
            return;
        }

        // order matters: scan from 0 each time
        for (int i = 0; i < (int)nums.size(); i++)
        {
            if (used[i]) continue;

            used[i] = true;
            path.push_back(nums[i]);
            explore();
            path.pop_back();

        }
    };

    explore();
    return result;
}
func permute(nums []int) [][]int {
	result := [][]int{}
	path := []int{}
	used := make([]bool, len(nums))

	var explore func()
	explore = func() {
		if len(path) == len(nums) {
			result = append(result, slices.Clone(path))
			return
		}

		for i := 0; i < len(nums); i++ { // order matters: scan from 0 each time
			if used[i] {
				continue
			}

			used[i] = true
			path = append(path, nums[i])
			explore()
			path = path[:len(path)-1]
			used[i] = false
		}
	}

	explore()
	return result
}
pub fn permute(nums: &[i32]) -> Vec<Vec<i32>> {
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    let mut path = Vec::new();
    let mut used = vec![false; nums.len()];

    explore_permutations(nums, &mut path, &mut used, &mut result);
    result
}

fn explore_permutations(
    nums: &[i32],
    path: &mut Vec<i32>,
    used: &mut [bool],
    result: &mut Vec<Vec<i32>>,
) {
    if path.len() == nums.len() {
        result.push(path.clone());
        return;
    }

    for i in 0..nums.len() {                     // order matters: scan from 0 each time
        if used[i] { continue; }

        used[i] = true;
        path.push(nums[i]);
        explore_permutations(nums, path, used, result);
        path.pop();
        used[i] = false;
    }
}

Time O(n · n!) · Space O(n) besides the output

Combination Sum#39Medium

Every combination that sums to target; a number may be reused.

function combinationSum(candidates: number[], target: number): number[][] {
  const result: number[][] = [];
  const path: number[] = [];
  candidates.sort((a, b) => a - b);  // sorted, so a branch can stop early

  function explore(start: number, remaining: number): void {
    if (remaining === 0) {
      result.push([...path]);
      return;
    }

    for (let i = start; i < candidates.length; i++) {
      if (candidates[i] > remaining) break;   // the rest are bigger still
      path.push(candidates[i]);
      explore(i, remaining - candidates[i]);  // i, not i + 1: reuse
      path.pop();
    }
  }

  explore(0, target);
  return result;
}
def combination_sum(candidates: list[int], target: int) -> list[list[int]]:
    result: list[list[int]] = []
    path: list[int] = []
    candidates.sort()                          # sorted, so a branch can stop early

    def explore(start: int, remaining: int) -> None:
        if remaining == 0:
            result.append(path.copy())
            return

        for i in range(start, len(candidates)):
            if candidates[i] > remaining:
                break

            path.append(candidates[i])
            explore(i, remaining - candidates[i])  # i, not i + 1: reuse allowed
            path.pop()

    explore(0, target)
    return result
public List<List<Integer>> combinationSum(int[] candidates, int target) {
    List<List<Integer>> result = new ArrayList<>();
    Arrays.sort(candidates);                   // sorted, so a branch can stop early
    exploreCombinations(candidates, target, 0, new ArrayList<>(), result);
    return result;
}

private static void exploreCombinations(int[] candidates, int remaining, int start,
                                        List<Integer> path, List<List<Integer>> result) {
    if (remaining == 0) {
        result.add(new ArrayList<>(path));
        return;
    }

    for (int i = start; i < candidates.length && candidates[i] <= remaining; i++) {
        path.add(candidates[i]);
        // pass i, not i + 1: the same number may be reused
        exploreCombinations(candidates, remaining - candidates[i], i, path, result);
        path.remove(path.size() - 1);
    }
}
public IList<IList<int>> CombinationSum(int[] candidates, int target)
{
    var result = new List<IList<int>>();
    var path = new List<int>();
    Array.Sort(candidates);                      // sorted, so a branch can stop early

    void Explore(int start, int remaining)
    {
        if (remaining == 0)
        {
            result.Add([.. path]);
            return;
        }

        for (int i = start; i < candidates.Length && candidates[i] <= remaining; i++)
        {
            path.Add(candidates[i]);
            Explore(i, remaining - candidates[i]);   // i, not i + 1: reuse allowed
            path.RemoveAt(path.Count - 1);
        }
    }

    Explore(0, target);
    return result;
}
let combinationSum (candidates: int[]) (target: int) : IList<IList<int>> =
    let result = ResizeArray<IList<int>>()
    let path = ResizeArray<int>()
    Array.sortInPlace candidates                    // sorted, so a branch can stop early

    let rec explore start remaining =
        if remaining = 0 then
            result.Add(path.ToArray() :> IList<int>)
        else
            for i in start .. candidates.Length - 1 do
                if candidates[i] <= remaining then
                    path.Add candidates[i]
                    explore i (remaining - candidates[i])   // i, not i + 1: reuse allowed
                    path.RemoveAt(path.Count - 1)

    explore 0 target
    result :> IList<IList<int>>

{

    vector<int> path;
    sort(candidates.begin(), candidates.end());    // sorted, so a branch can stop early

    function<void(int, int)> explore = [&](int start, int remaining)
    {
        if (remaining == 0)
        {
            result.push_back(path);
            return;
        }

        for (int i = start; i < (int)candidates.size() && candidates[i] <= remaining; i++)
        {
            path.push_back(candidates[i]);
            explore(i, remaining - candidates[i]);  // i, not i + 1: reuse allowed
            path.pop_back();
        }
    };

    explore(0, target);
    return result;
}
func combinationSum(candidates []int, target int) [][]int {
	result := [][]int{}
	path := []int{}
	sort.Ints(candidates) // sorted, so a branch can stop early

	var explore func(start, remaining int)
	explore = func(start, remaining int) {
		if remaining == 0 {
			result = append(result, slices.Clone(path))
			return
		}

		for i := start; i < len(candidates) && candidates[i] <= remaining; i++ {
			path = append(path, candidates[i])
			explore(i, remaining-candidates[i]) // i, not i + 1: reuse allowed
			path = path[:len(path)-1]
		}
	}

	explore(0, target)
	return result
}
pub fn combination_sum(candidates: &[i32], target: i32) -> Vec<Vec<i32>> {
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    let mut path = Vec::new();
    let mut candidates = candidates.to_vec();
    candidates.sort_unstable();                  // sorted, so a branch can stop early

    explore_combinations(&candidates, 0, target, &mut path, &mut result);
    result
}

fn explore_combinations(
    candidates: &[i32],
    start: usize,
    remaining: i32,
    path: &mut Vec<i32>,
    result: &mut Vec<Vec<i32>>,
) {
    if remaining == 0 {
        result.push(path.clone());
        return;
    }

    for i in start..candidates.len() {
        if candidates[i] > remaining { break; }

        path.push(candidates[i]);
        explore_combinations(candidates, i, remaining - candidates[i], path, result);
        path.pop();                              // i, not i + 1: reuse allowed
    }
}

Time exponential, cut down by the sorted early stop · Space O(target / smallest candidate) for the recursion

Dynamic programming

Recursion & DP

Use it when you count the ways, find a min or max cost, or decide "is it possible?", and the same subproblems keep coming back. Comparing two strings or sequences is almost always DP.

How it works

  • Define the state in words: dp[i] is the best answer for the first i items (or from i onward).
  • Write the recurrence: the choice at i in terms of smaller states, plus the base cases.
  • Top-down is recursion plus a memo, the easiest to get right. Bottom-up fills a table in an order where every dependency comes first.
  • Common shapes: 1D (house robber, coin change, LIS), two strings (LCS, edit distance), grid paths, 0/1 knapsack.

Watch out

  • Get a correct memoized version first; shrink the space afterwards.
  • Pick sentinels that can't overflow: amount + 1, not the largest int, when you'll add 1 to it.

House Robber#198Medium

The largest sum of houses with no two neighbors robbed. Shown both ways, so you can see the recursion turn into a loop.

// 1. Top-down: write the recursion, then cache it.
function robMemo(nums: number[]): number {
  const memo: (number | undefined)[] = [];

  function best(i: number): number {  // the most loot from house i on
    if (i >= nums.length) return 0;
    return memo[i] ??= Math.max(
      best(i + 1),                    // skip house i
      nums[i] + best(i + 2),          // rob it and skip its neighbor
    );
  }

  return best(0);
}

// 2. Bottom-up: the same recurrence, from the end, two values kept.
function rob(nums: number[]): number {
  let next1 = 0, next2 = 0;  // best(i + 1) and best(i + 2)

  for (let i = nums.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const best = Math.max(next1, nums[i] + next2);
    next2 = next1;
    next1 = best;
  }

  return next1;
}
# 1. Top-down: write the recursion, then cache it.
def rob_memo(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    memo: list[int | None] = [None] * len(nums)

    def best(i: int) -> int:                   # most loot from house i onward
        if i >= len(nums):
            return 0

        if memo[i] is None:
            memo[i] = max(
                best(i + 1),                   # skip house i
                nums[i] + best(i + 2),         # rob it and skip its neighbor
            )
        return memo[i]

    return best(0)


# 2. Bottom-up: same recurrence, filled from the end, keeping only two values.
def rob(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    next1 = next2 = 0                          # Best(i + 1) and Best(i + 2)

    for i in range(len(nums) - 1, -1, -1):
        best = max(next1, nums[i] + next2)
        next2 = next1
        next1 = best

    return next1
// 1. Top-down: write the recursion, then cache it.
public int robMemo(int[] nums) {
    return best(nums, 0, new Integer[nums.length]);
}

private static int best(int[] nums, int i, Integer[] memo) {   // most loot from house i onward
    if (i >= nums.length) return 0;
    if (memo[i] != null) return memo[i];

    memo[i] = Math.max(
        best(nums, i + 1, memo),               // skip house i
        nums[i] + best(nums, i + 2, memo));    // rob it and skip its neighbor
    return memo[i];
}

// 2. Bottom-up: same recurrence, filled from the end, keeping only two values.
public int rob(int[] nums) {
    int next1 = 0, next2 = 0;                  // Best(i + 1) and Best(i + 2)

    for (int i = nums.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        int best = Math.max(next1, nums[i] + next2);
        next2 = next1;
        next1 = best;
    }

    return next1;
}
// 1. Top-down: write the recursion, then cache it.
public int RobMemo(int[] nums)
{
    var memo = new int?[nums.Length];

    int Best(int i)                              // most loot from house i onward
    {
        if (i >= nums.Length) return 0;
        return memo[i] ??= Math.Max(
            Best(i + 1),                         // skip house i
            nums[i] + Best(i + 2));              // rob it and skip its neighbor
    }

    return Best(0);
}

// 2. Bottom-up: same recurrence, filled from the end, keeping only two values.
public int Rob(int[] nums)
{
    int next1 = 0, next2 = 0;                    // Best(i + 1) and Best(i + 2)

    for (int i = nums.Length - 1; i >= 0; i--)
    {
        int best = Math.Max(next1, nums[i] + next2);
        next2 = next1;
        next1 = best;
    }

    return next1;
}
// 1. Top-down: write the recursion, then cache it.
let robMemo (nums: int[]) : int =
    let memo : int option[] = Array.create nums.Length None

    let rec best i =                            // most loot from house i onward
        if i >= nums.Length then 0
        else
            match memo[i] with
            | Some v -> v
            | None ->
                let skip = best (i + 1)         // skip house i
                let take = nums[i] + best (i + 2)   // rob it and skip its neighbor
                let v = max skip take
                memo[i] <- Some v
                v

    best 0

// 2. Bottom-up: same recurrence, filled from the end, keeping only two values.
let rob (nums: int[]) : int =
    let mutable next1 = 0                       // Best(i + 1) and Best(i + 2)
    let mutable next2 = 0

    for i in nums.Length - 1 .. -1 .. 0 do
        let best = max next1 (nums[i] + next2)
        next2 <- next1
        next1 <- best

    next1
// 1. Top-down: write the recursion, then cache it.
int robMemo(vector<int>& nums)
{
    vector<optional<int>> memo(nums.size());

    function<int(int)> best = [&](int i) -> int    // most loot from house i onward
    {
        if (i >= (int)nums.size()) return 0;
        if (!memo[i])
            memo[i] = max(best(i + 1),             // skip house i
                          nums[i] + best(i + 2));  // rob it and skip its neighbor
        return *memo[i];
    };

    return best(0);
}

// 2. Bottom-up: same recurrence, filled from the end, keeping only two values.
int rob(vector<int>& nums)
{
    int next1 = 0, next2 = 0;                      // Best(i + 1) and Best(i + 2)

    for (int i = (int)nums.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--)
    {
        int best = max(next1, nums[i] + next2);
        next2 = next1;
        next1 = best;
    }

    return next1;
}
// 1. Top-down: write the recursion, then cache it.
func robMemo(nums []int) int {
	memo := make([]int, len(nums))
	for i := range memo {
		memo[i] = -1 // -1: not computed yet, and loot is never negative
	}

	var best func(i int) int // most loot from house i onward
	best = func(i int) int {
		if i >= len(nums) {
			return 0
		}
		if memo[i] < 0 {
			memo[i] = max(
				best(i+1),         // skip house i
				nums[i]+best(i+2)) // rob it and skip its neighbor
		}
		return memo[i]
	}

	return best(0)
}

// 2. Bottom-up: same recurrence, filled from the end, keeping only two values.
func rob(nums []int) int {
	next1, next2 := 0, 0 // Best(i + 1) and Best(i + 2)

	for i := len(nums) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		best := max(next1, nums[i]+next2)
		next1, next2 = best, next1
	}

	return next1
}
// 1. Top-down: write the recursion, then cache it.
pub fn rob_memo(nums: &[i32]) -> i32 {
    let mut memo = vec![None; nums.len()];
    best_loot(nums, 0, &mut memo)
}

fn best_loot(nums: &[i32], i: usize, memo: &mut Vec<Option<i32>>) -> i32 {
    if i >= nums.len() { return 0; }            // most loot from house i onward
    if let Some(best) = memo[i] { return best; }

    let best = best_loot(nums, i + 1, memo)             // skip house i
        .max(nums[i] + best_loot(nums, i + 2, memo));   // rob it and skip its neighbor
    memo[i] = Some(best);
    best
}

// 2. Bottom-up: same recurrence, filled from the end, keeping only two values.
pub fn rob(nums: &[i32]) -> i32 {
    let (mut next1, mut next2) = (0, 0);         // Best(i + 1) and Best(i + 2)

    for &num in nums.iter().rev() {
        let best = next1.max(num + next2);
        next2 = next1;
        next1 = best;
    }

    next1
}

Time O(n) · Space O(n) with the memo, O(1) bottom-up

Coin Change#322Medium

The fewest coins that make amount, or -1 if no combination does.

function coinChange(coins: number[], amount: number): number {
  // dp[a] = the fewest coins that make a; Infinity means "can't yet"
  const dp: number[] = new Array(amount + 1).fill(Infinity);
  dp[0] = 0;

  for (let a = 1; a <= amount; a++)
    for (const coin of coins)
      if (coin <= a)
        dp[a] = Math.min(dp[a], dp[a - coin] + 1);  // use coin last

  return dp[amount] === Infinity ? -1 : dp[amount];
}
def coin_change(coins: list[int], amount: int) -> int:
    infinity = amount + 1                      # "infinity" that can't overflow
    dp = [infinity] * (amount + 1)             # dp[a] = fewest coins that make a
    dp[0] = 0

    for a in range(1, amount + 1):
        for coin in coins:
            if coin <= a:
                dp[a] = min(dp[a], dp[a - coin] + 1)  # use coin last

    return dp[amount] if dp[amount] != infinity else -1
public int coinChange(int[] coins, int amount) {
    int[] dp = new int[amount + 1];            // dp[a] = fewest coins that make a
    Arrays.fill(dp, amount + 1);               // "infinity" that can't overflow
    dp[0] = 0;

    for (int a = 1; a <= amount; a++)
        for (int coin : coins)
            if (coin <= a)
                dp[a] = Math.min(dp[a], dp[a - coin] + 1);   // use coin last

    return dp[amount] > amount ? -1 : dp[amount];
}
public int CoinChange(int[] coins, int amount)
{
    var dp = new int[amount + 1];                // dp[a] = fewest coins that make a
    Array.Fill(dp, amount + 1);                  // "infinity" that can't overflow
    dp[0] = 0;

    for (int a = 1; a <= amount; a++)
        foreach (int coin in coins)
            if (coin <= a)
                dp[a] = Math.Min(dp[a], dp[a - coin] + 1);   // use coin last

    return dp[amount] > amount ? -1 : dp[amount];
}
let coinChange (coins: int[]) (amount: int) : int =
    let infinity = amount + 1                             // "infinity" that can't overflow
    let dp = Array.create (amount + 1) infinity           // dp[a] = fewest coins that make a
    dp[0] <- 0

    for a in 1 .. amount do
        for coin in coins do
            if coin <= a then
                dp[a] <- min dp[a] (dp[a - coin] + 1)   // use coin last

    if dp[amount] > amount then -1 else dp[amount]
int coinChange(vector<int>& coins, int amount)
{
    // dp[a] = fewest coins that make a
    // amount + 1 is an "infinity" that can't overflow
    vector<int> dp(amount + 1, amount + 1);
    dp[0] = 0;

    for (int a = 1; a <= amount; a++)
        for (int coin : coins)
            if (coin <= a)
                dp[a] = min(dp[a], dp[a - coin] + 1);   // use coin last

    return dp[amount] > amount ? -1 : dp[amount];
}
func coinChange(coins []int, amount int) int {
	dp := make([]int, amount+1) // dp[a] = fewest coins that make a
	for a := range dp {
		dp[a] = amount + 1 // "infinity" that can't overflow
	}
	dp[0] = 0

	for a := 1; a <= amount; a++ {
		for _, coin := range coins {
			if coin <= a {
				dp[a] = min(dp[a], dp[a-coin]+1) // use coin last
			}
		}
	}

	if dp[amount] > amount {
		return -1
	}
	return dp[amount]
}
pub fn coin_change(coins: &[i32], amount: i32) -> i32 {
    let target = amount as usize;
    // dp[a] = fewest coins that make a. amount + 1 is an "infinity" that cannot overflow.
    let mut dp = vec![amount + 1; target + 1];
    dp[0] = 0;

    for a in 1..=target {
        for &coin in coins {
            let coin = coin as usize;
            if coin <= a {
                dp[a] = dp[a].min(dp[a - coin] + 1);   // use coin last
            }
        }
    }

    if dp[target] > amount { -1 } else { dp[target] }
}

Time O(amount · coins) · Space O(amount)

Longest Common Subsequence#1143Medium

The length of the longest subsequence two strings share. The table in the diagram is this code's dp.

function longestCommonSubsequence(text1: string, text2: string): number {
  const m = text1.length, n = text2.length;
  // dp[i][j]: the first i chars of text1 against the first j of text2
  const dp: number[][] = Array.from(
    { length: m + 1 },
    () => new Array(n + 1).fill(0),  // a new row for every i
  );

  for (let i = 1; i <= m; i++)
    for (let j = 1; j <= n; j++)
      dp[i][j] = text1[i - 1] === text2[j - 1]
        ? dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1                   // match: extend diagonal
        : Math.max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]);  // drop a char

  return dp[m][n];
}
def longest_common_subsequence(text1: str, text2: str) -> int:
    m, n = len(text1), len(text2)
    dp = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(m + 1)]  # dp[i][j]: first i chars vs first j

    for i in range(1, m + 1):
        for j in range(1, n + 1):
            if text1[i - 1] == text2[j - 1]:
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1  # match: extend the diagonal
            else:
                dp[i][j] = max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1])  # drop a char from one side

    return dp[m][n]
public int longestCommonSubsequence(String text1, String text2) {
    int m = text1.length(), n = text2.length();
    int[][] dp = new int[m + 1][n + 1];        // dp[i][j]: first i chars vs first j

    for (int i = 1; i <= m; i++) {
        for (int j = 1; j <= n; j++) {
            dp[i][j] = text1.charAt(i - 1) == text2.charAt(j - 1)
                ? dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1                     // match: extend the diagonal
                : Math.max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]);    // drop a char from one side
        }
    }

    return dp[m][n];
}
public int LongestCommonSubsequence(string text1, string text2)
{
    int m = text1.Length, n = text2.Length;
    var dp = new int[m + 1, n + 1];              // dp[i, j]: first i chars vs first j

    for (int i = 1; i <= m; i++)
    {
        for (int j = 1; j <= n; j++)
        {
            dp[i, j] = text1[i - 1] == text2[j - 1]
                ? dp[i - 1, j - 1] + 1                   // match: extend the diagonal
                : Math.Max(dp[i - 1, j], dp[i, j - 1]);  // drop a char from one side
        }
    }

    return dp[m, n];
}
let longestCommonSubsequence (text1: string) (text2: string) : int =
    let m = text1.Length
    let n = text2.Length
    let dp = Array2D.zeroCreate<int> (m + 1) (n + 1)   // dp[i, j]: first i chars vs first j

    for i in 1 .. m do
        for j in 1 .. n do
            dp[i, j] <-
                if text1[i - 1] = text2[j - 1] then
                    dp[i - 1, j - 1] + 1                    // match: extend the diagonal
                else
                    max (dp[i - 1, j]) (dp[i, j - 1])       // drop a char from one side

    dp[m, n]
int longestCommonSubsequence(string text1, string text2)
{
    int m = (int)text1.size(), n = (int)text2.size();
    vector<vector<int>> dp(m + 1, vector<int>(n + 1, 0));   // dp[i][j]: first i vs first j

    for (int i = 1; i <= m; i++)
    {
        for (int j = 1; j <= n; j++)
        {
            dp[i][j] = text1[i - 1] == text2[j - 1]
                ? dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1             // match: extend the diagonal
                : max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1]);  // drop a char from one side
        }
    }

    return dp[m][n];
}
func longestCommonSubsequence(text1 string, text2 string) int {
	m, n := len(text1), len(text2)
	dp := make([][]int, m+1) // dp[i][j]: first i chars vs first j
	for i := range dp {
		dp[i] = make([]int, n+1)
	}

	for i := 1; i <= m; i++ {
		for j := 1; j <= n; j++ {
			if text1[i-1] == text2[j-1] {
				dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 // match: extend the diagonal
			} else {
				dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]) // drop a char from one side
			}
		}
	}

	return dp[m][n]
}
pub fn longest_common_subsequence(text1: &str, text2: &str) -> i32 {
    let (m, n) = (text1.len(), text2.len());
    let (a, b) = (text1.as_bytes(), text2.as_bytes());
    let mut dp = vec![vec![0; n + 1]; m + 1];    // dp[i][j]: first i chars vs first j

    for i in 1..=m {
        for j in 1..=n {
            dp[i][j] = if a[i - 1] == b[j - 1] {
                dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1                // match: extend the diagonal
            } else {
                dp[i - 1][j].max(dp[i][j - 1])      // drop a char from one side
            };
        }
    }

    dp[m][n]
}

Time O(m · n) · Space O(m · n)

14

Intervals / greedy

Greedy

Use it when you see start and end pairs, meetings, overlaps, merging ranges, "the fewest to remove or cover", or how far you can reach.

How it works

  • Sort first: by start to merge, by end to keep the most intervals that don't overlap.
  • Two intervals overlap when a.start <= b.end and b.start <= a.end.
  • Greedy: make the locally best choice (the interval that ends first, the farthest reach) when you can argue it never hurts.

Watch out

  • Check whether touching endpoints ([1, 2] and [2, 3]) count as overlapping. Problems differ.
  • If you can't justify the greedy choice, it's probably DP.

Merge Intervals#56Mediumdojo 02

Merge every set of overlapping intervals.

function merge(intervals: number[][]): number[][] {
  intervals.sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0]);  // by start
  const merged: number[][] = [];

  for (const [start, end] of intervals) {
    const last = merged.at(-1);
    if (last !== undefined && start <= last[1])
      last[1] = Math.max(last[1], end);  // overlap: extend
    else
      merged.push([start, end]);         // gap: start a new one
  }

  return merged;
}
def merge(intervals: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]:
    intervals.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[0])   # by start
    merged: list[list[int]] = []

    for current in intervals:
        if merged and current[0] <= merged[-1][1]:
            merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], current[1])  # overlap: extend
        else:
            merged.append([current[0], current[1]])  # gap: start new

    return merged
public int[][] merge(int[][] intervals) {
    Arrays.sort(intervals, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[0], b[0]));   // by start
    List<int[]> merged = new ArrayList<>();

    for (int[] current : intervals) {
        int[] last = merged.isEmpty() ? null : merged.get(merged.size() - 1);

        if (last != null && current[0] <= last[1])
            last[1] = Math.max(last[1], current[1]);          // overlap: extend
        else
            merged.add(new int[] {current[0], current[1]});   // gap: start new
    }

    return merged.toArray(new int[0][]);
}
public int[][] Merge(int[][] intervals)
{
    Array.Sort(intervals, (a, b) => a[0].CompareTo(b[0]));   // by start
    var merged = new List<int[]>();

    foreach (int[] current in intervals)
    {
        if (merged.Count > 0 && current[0] <= merged[^1][1])
            merged[^1][1] = Math.Max(merged[^1][1], current[1]);   // overlap: extend
        else
            merged.Add([current[0], current[1]]);                   // gap: start new
    }

    return merged.ToArray();
}
let merge (intervals: int[][]) : int[][] =
    Array.sortInPlaceBy (fun (a: int[]) -> a[0]) intervals   // by start
    let merged = ResizeArray<int[]>()

    for current in intervals do
        if merged.Count > 0 && current[0] <= merged[merged.Count - 1][1] then
            let last = merged[merged.Count - 1]
            last[1] <- max last[1] current[1]           // overlap: extend
        else
            merged.Add(Array.copy current)              // gap: start new

    merged.ToArray()
vector<vector<int>> merge(vector<vector<int>>& intervals)
{
    sort(intervals.begin(), intervals.end(),
         [](const vector<int>& a, const vector<int>& b) { return a[0] < b[0]; });   // by start
    vector<vector<int>> merged;

    for (auto& current : intervals)
    {
        if (!merged.empty() && current[0] <= merged.back()[1])
            merged.back()[1] = max(merged.back()[1], current[1]);   // overlap: extend
        else
            merged.push_back(current);             // gap: start new
    }

    return merged;
}
func merge(intervals [][]int) [][]int {
	sort.Slice(intervals, func(i, j int) bool {
		return intervals[i][0] < intervals[j][0] // by start
	})
	merged := [][]int{}

	for _, current := range intervals {
		last := len(merged) - 1
		if last >= 0 && current[0] <= merged[last][1] {
			merged[last][1] = max(merged[last][1], current[1]) // overlap: extend
		} else {
			merged = append(merged, []int{current[0], current[1]}) // gap: start new
		}
	}

	return merged
}
pub fn merge(mut intervals: Vec<Vec<i32>>) -> Vec<Vec<i32>> {
    intervals.sort_unstable_by_key(|interval| interval[0]);   // by start
    let mut merged: Vec<Vec<i32>> = Vec::new();

    for current in intervals {
        match merged.last_mut() {
            Some(last) if current[0] <= last[1] => {
                last[1] = last[1].max(current[1]);   // overlap: extend
            }
            _ => merged.push(current),               // gap: start new
        }
    }

    merged
}

Time O(n log n) · Space O(n)

Non-overlapping Intervals#435Medium

The fewest intervals to remove so the rest don't overlap. Keep whichever ends first: it leaves the most room.

function eraseOverlapIntervals(intervals: number[][]): number {
  intervals.sort((a, b) => a[1] - b[1]);  // by end
  let removed = 0, end = -Infinity;

  for (const [start, finish] of intervals) {
    if (start >= end) end = finish;  // fits after the last kept
    else removed++;                  // overlaps one that ends sooner
  }

  return removed;
}
def erase_overlap_intervals(intervals: list[list[int]]) -> int:
    intervals.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[1])   # by end
    removed, end = 0, float("-inf")

    for start, finish in intervals:
        if start >= end:
            end = finish                       # fits after the last kept: keep it
        else:
            removed += 1                       # overlaps one that ends sooner

    return removed
public int eraseOverlapIntervals(int[][] intervals) {
    Arrays.sort(intervals, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[1], b[1]));   // by end
    int removed = 0, end = Integer.MIN_VALUE;

    for (int[] interval : intervals) {
        if (interval[0] >= end) end = interval[1];   // fits after the last kept: keep it
        else removed++;                              // overlaps one that ends sooner
    }

    return removed;
}

func eraseOverlapIntervals(intervals [][]int) int {
	sort.Slice(intervals, func(i, j int) bool {
		return intervals[i][1] < intervals[j][1] // by end
	})
	removed, end := 0, math.MinInt

	for _, interval := range intervals {
		if interval[0] >= end {
			end = interval[1] // fits after the last kept: keep it
		} else {
			removed++ // overlaps one that ends sooner
		}
	}

	return removed
}
pub fn erase_overlap_intervals(mut intervals: Vec<Vec<i32>>) -> i32 {
    intervals.sort_unstable_by_key(|interval| interval[1]);   // by end
    let (mut removed, mut end) = (0, i32::MIN);

    for interval in &intervals {
        if interval[0] >= end { end = interval[1]; }   // fits after the last kept: keep it
        else { removed += 1; }                         // overlaps one that ends sooner
    }

    removed
}

Time O(n log n) · Space O(1) beyond the sort

Jump Game#55Medium

From index i you may jump up to nums[i]. Can you reach the last index?

function canJump(nums: number[]): boolean {
  let reach = 0;  // the farthest index we can get to

  for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) {
    if (i > reach) return false;  // stuck before i
    reach = Math.max(reach, i + nums[i]);
  }

  return true;
}

    for i, jump in enumerate(nums):
        if i > reach:
            return False                       # stuck before reaching i
        reach = max(reach, i + jump)

    return True

Union-Find

Trees & graphs less common

Use it when connectivity changes as you go: "are these connected?", merging groups (accounts, provinces), counting components as edges arrive, or the edge that closes a cycle in an undirected graph.

How it works

  • Every set is a tree. parent[x] points toward the root, and the root names the set.
  • Find climbs to the root and flattens the path on the way. Union links two roots.
  • With path compression and union by size, each operation is nearly O(1).

Watch out

  • Union links the roots, Find(a) and Find(b), never the nodes themselves.
  • Check whether nodes are numbered from 0 or 1 when you size the arrays.

Redundant Connection#684Medium

A tree with one extra edge: return the edge that creates the cycle. The UnionFind class is reusable as-is.

class UnionFind {
  private parent: number[];
  private size: number[];

  constructor(n: number) {
    this.parent = Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => i);  // all roots
    this.size = new Array(n).fill(1);
  }

  find(x: number): number {
    while (this.parent[x] !== x) {
      this.parent[x] = this.parent[this.parent[x]];  // path halving
      x = this.parent[x];
    }
    return x;
  }

  union(a: number, b: number): boolean {  // false if already joined
    let rootA = this.find(a), rootB = this.find(b);
    if (rootA === rootB) return false;

    if (this.size[rootA] < this.size[rootB])
      [rootA, rootB] = [rootB, rootA];  // keep rootA the bigger tree
    this.parent[rootB] = rootA;         // hang the smaller tree under it
    this.size[rootA] += this.size[rootB];
    return true;
  }
}

function findRedundantConnection(edges: number[][]): number[] {
  const sets = new UnionFind(edges.length + 1);  // nodes are 1..n
  for (const [a, b] of edges)
    if (!sets.union(a, b)) return [a, b];        // this edge closes a cycle
  return [];
}
class UnionFind:
    def __init__(self, n: int):
        self.parent = list(range(n))           # everyone starts as a root
        self.size = [1] * n

    def find(self, x: int) -> int:
        while self.parent[x] != x:
            self.parent[x] = self.parent[self.parent[x]]  # path halving keeps trees flat
            x = self.parent[x]
        return x

    def union(self, a: int, b: int) -> bool:   # false if already connected
        root_a, root_b = self.find(a), self.find(b)
        if root_a == root_b:
            return False

        if self.size[root_a] < self.size[root_b]:
            root_a, root_b = root_b, root_a
        self.parent[root_b] = root_a           # hang the smaller tree under the bigger
        self.size[root_a] += self.size[root_b]
        return True


def find_redundant_connection(edges: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
    sets = UnionFind(len(edges) + 1)           # nodes are numbered 1..n
    for a, b in edges:
        if not sets.union(a, b):
            return [a, b]                      # closes a cycle
    return []
public class UnionFind {
    private final int[] parent;
    private final int[] size;

    public UnionFind(int n) {
        parent = new int[n];
        size = new int[n];
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) parent[i] = i;   // everyone starts as a root
        Arrays.fill(size, 1);
    }

    public int find(int x) {
        while (parent[x] != x) {
            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]];     // path halving keeps trees flat
            x = parent[x];
        }
        return x;
    }

    public boolean union(int a, int b) {       // false if already connected
        int rootA = find(a), rootB = find(b);
        if (rootA == rootB) return false;

        if (size[rootA] < size[rootB]) {
            int swap = rootA;
            rootA = rootB;
            rootB = swap;
        }
        parent[rootB] = rootA;                 // hang the smaller tree under the bigger
        size[rootA] += size[rootB];
        return true;
    }
}

public int[] findRedundantConnection(int[][] edges) {
    UnionFind sets = new UnionFind(edges.length + 1);   // nodes are numbered 1..n
    for (int[] edge : edges)
        if (!sets.union(edge[0], edge[1])) return edge;   // closes a cycle
    return new int[0];
}
