type UnionFind(n: int) =
    let parent = Array.init n id                // everyone starts as a root
    let size = Array.create n 1

    member _.Find(x: int) =
        let mutable node = x
        while parent[node] <> node do
            parent[node] <- parent[parent[node]]   // path halving keeps trees flat
            node <- parent[node]
        node

    member this.Union(a: int, b: int) =         // false if already connected
        let mutable rootA = this.Find a
        let mutable rootB = this.Find b

        if rootA = rootB then false
        else
            if size[rootA] < size[rootB] then
                let swap = rootA
                rootA <- rootB
                rootB <- swap

            parent[rootB] <- rootA              // hang the smaller tree under the bigger
            size[rootA] <- size[rootA] + size[rootB]
            true

let findRedundantConnection (edges: int[][]) : int[] =
    let sets = UnionFind(edges.Length + 1)      // nodes are numbered 1..n

    let rec search i =
        if i = edges.Length then [||]
        elif not (sets.Union(edges[i][0], edges[i][1])) then edges[i]   // closes a cycle
        else search (i + 1)

    search 0
class UnionFind
{
    vector<int> parent;
    vector<int> size;

public:
    UnionFind(int n) : parent(n), size(n, 1)
    {
        iota(parent.begin(), parent.end(), 0);     // everyone starts as a root
    }

    int find(int x)
    {
        while (parent[x] != x)
        {
            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]];         // path halving keeps trees flat
            x = parent[x];
        }
        return x;
    }

    bool unite(int a, int b)                       // false if already connected
    {
        int rootA = find(a), rootB = find(b);
        if (rootA == rootB) return false;

        if (size[rootA] < size[rootB]) swap(rootA, rootB);
        parent[rootB] = rootA;                     // hang the smaller tree under the bigger
        size[rootA] += size[rootB];
        return true;
    }
};

vector<int> findRedundantConnection(vector<vector<int>>& edges)
{
    UnionFind sets((int)edges.size() + 1);         // nodes are numbered 1..n
    for (auto& edge : edges)
        if (!sets.unite(edge[0], edge[1])) return edge;   // closes a cycle
    return {};
}
type UnionFind struct {
	parent []int
	size   []int
}

func newUnionFind(n int) UnionFind {
	parent := make([]int, n)
	size := make([]int, n)
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		parent[i] = i // everyone starts as a root
	}
	for i := range size {
		size[i] = 1
	}
	return UnionFind{parent: parent, size: size}
}

func (u *UnionFind) find(x int) int {
	for u.parent[x] != x {
		u.parent[x] = u.parent[u.parent[x]] // path halving keeps trees flat
		x = u.parent[x]
	}
	return x
}

func (u *UnionFind) union(a, b int) bool { // false if already connected
	rootA, rootB := u.find(a), u.find(b)
	if rootA == rootB {
		return false
	}

	if u.size[rootA] < u.size[rootB] {
		rootA, rootB = rootB, rootA
	}
	u.parent[rootB] = rootA // hang the smaller tree under the bigger
	u.size[rootA] += u.size[rootB]
	return true
}

func findRedundantConnection(edges [][]int) []int {
	sets := newUnionFind(len(edges) + 1) // nodes are numbered 1..n
	for _, edge := range edges {
		if !sets.union(edge[0], edge[1]) {
			return edge // closes a cycle
		}
	}
	return []int{}
}
pub struct UnionFind {
    parent: Vec<usize>,
    size: Vec<usize>,
}

impl UnionFind {
    pub fn new(n: usize) -> Self {
        UnionFind {
            parent: (0..n).collect(),            // everyone starts as a root
            size: vec![1; n],
        }
    }

    pub fn find(&mut self, mut x: usize) -> usize {
        while self.parent[x] != x {
            self.parent[x] = self.parent[self.parent[x]];   // path halving keeps trees flat
            x = self.parent[x];
        }
        x
    }

    pub fn union(&mut self, a: usize, b: usize) -> bool {   // false if already connected
        let (mut root_a, mut root_b) = (self.find(a), self.find(b));
        if root_a == root_b { return false; }

        if self.size[root_a] < self.size[root_b] {
            std::mem::swap(&mut root_a, &mut root_b);
        }
        self.parent[root_b] = root_a;            // hang the smaller tree under the bigger
        self.size[root_a] += self.size[root_b];
        true
    }
}

pub fn find_redundant_connection(edges: &[Vec<i32>]) -> Vec<i32> {
    let mut sets = UnionFind::new(edges.len() + 1);   // nodes are numbered 1..n
    for edge in edges {
        if !sets.union(edge[0] as usize, edge[1] as usize) {
            return edge.clone();                 // closes a cycle
        }
    }
    Vec::new()
}

Time O(n · α(n)), effectively O(n) · Space O(n)

Trie

Data structures less common

Use it when the problem is about prefixes, autocomplete, "starts with", many lookups against the same word list, or searching a board for many words at once.

How it works

  • Each node has up to 26 children, one per letter; a path from the root spells a prefix.
  • Mark the node where a word ends.
  • Insert and search cost O(word length), however many words are stored.

Watch out

  • Search needs the end-of-word flag; StartsWith doesn't.
  • Use a hash map from character to node for the children when the alphabet isn't just a to z.

Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)#208Medium

Insert words, then search for a whole word or a prefix.

class TrieNode {
  children = new Map<string, TrieNode>();  // letter -> child
  isWord = false;
}

class Trie {
  private root = new TrieNode();

  insert(word: string): void {
    let node = this.root;
    for (const ch of word) {
      const next = node.children.get(ch) ?? new TrieNode();
      node.children.set(ch, next);  // no change if it was there
      node = next;
    }
    node.isWord = true;
  }

  search(word: string): boolean {
    return this.walk(word)?.isWord === true;
  }

  startsWith(prefix: string): boolean {
    return this.walk(prefix) !== null;
  }

  private walk(s: string): TrieNode | null {  // null if it falls off
    let node = this.root;
    for (const ch of s) {
      const next = node.children.get(ch);
      if (next === undefined) return null;
      node = next;
    }
    return node;
  }
}
class Trie:
    class Node:
        def __init__(self):
            self.children: dict[str, Trie.Node] = {}  # one slot per letter seen
            self.is_word = False

    def __init__(self):
        self.root = Trie.Node()

    def insert(self, word: str) -> None:
        node = self.root
        for ch in word:
            node = node.children.setdefault(ch, Trie.Node())
        node.is_word = True

    def search(self, word: str) -> bool:
        node = self._walk(word)
        return node is not None and node.is_word

    def starts_with(self, prefix: str) -> bool:
        return self._walk(prefix) is not None

    def _walk(self, s: str) -> Trie.Node | None:  # follow s from the root, None if it falls off
        node = self.root
        for ch in s:
            node = node.children.get(ch)
            if node is None:
                return None
        return node
public class Trie {
    private static class Node {
        Node[] next = new Node[26];            // one slot per letter
        boolean isWord;
    }

    private final Node root = new Node();

    public void insert(String word) {
        Node node = root;
        for (char ch : word.toCharArray()) {
            int slot = ch - 'a';
            if (node.next[slot] == null) node.next[slot] = new Node();
            node = node.next[slot];
        }
        node.isWord = true;
    }

    public boolean search(String word) {
        Node node = walk(word);
        return node != null && node.isWord;
    }

    public boolean startsWith(String prefix) {
        return walk(prefix) != null;
    }

    private Node walk(String s) {              // follow s from the root; null if it falls off
        Node node = root;
        for (char ch : s.toCharArray()) {
            node = node.next[ch - 'a'];
            if (node == null) return null;
        }
        return node;
    }
}
public class Trie
{
    private class Node
    {
        public readonly Node[] Next = new Node[26];   // one slot per letter
        public bool IsWord;
    }

    private readonly Node root = new();

    public void Insert(string word)
    {
        Node node = root;
        foreach (char ch in word)
            node = node.Next[ch - 'a'] ??= new Node();
        node.IsWord = true;
    }

    public bool Search(string word) => Walk(word)?.IsWord == true;

    public bool StartsWith(string prefix) => Walk(prefix) != null;

    private Node Walk(string s)                  // follow s from the root, null if it falls off
    {
        Node node = root;
        foreach (char ch in s)
        {
            node = node.Next[ch - 'a'];
            if (node == null) return null;
        }
        return node;
    }
}
// The trie's own node, kept beside it because F# has no nested types.
type TrieNode() =
    member val Next : TrieNode option[] = Array.create 26 None   // one slot per letter
    member val IsWord = false with get, set

type Trie() =
    let root = TrieNode()

    member _.Insert(word: string) =
        let mutable node = root
        for ch in word do
            match node.Next[int ch - int 'a'] with
            | Some next -> node <- next
            | None ->
                let next = TrieNode()
                node.Next[int ch - int 'a'] <- Some next
                node <- next
        node.IsWord <- true

    member this.Search(word: string) =
        match this.Walk word with
        | Some node -> node.IsWord
        | None -> false

    member this.StartsWith(prefix: string) = (this.Walk prefix).IsSome

    member _.Walk(s: string) : TrieNode option =   // follow s from the root, None if it falls off
        let mutable node = Some root
        let mutable i = 0
        while node.IsSome && i < s.Length do
            node <- node.Value.Next[int s[i] - int 'a']
            i <- i + 1
        node
class Trie
{
    struct Node
    {
        Node* next[26] = {};                       // one slot per letter, null until used
        bool isWord = false;
    };

    Node* root = new Node();

    Node* walk(const string& s)                    // follow s from the root, null if it falls off
    {
        Node* node = root;
        for (char ch : s)
        {
            node = node->next[ch - 'a'];
            if (!node) return nullptr;
        }
        return node;
    }

public:
    void insert(string word)
    {
        Node* node = root;
        for (char ch : word)
        {
            Node*& slot = node->next[ch - 'a'];
            if (!slot) slot = new Node();
            node = slot;
        }
        node->isWord = true;
    }

    bool search(string word) { Node* node = walk(word); return node && node->isWord; }

    bool startsWith(string prefix) { return walk(prefix) != nullptr; }
};
type Trie struct {
	root *trieNode
}

type trieNode struct {
	next   [26]*trieNode // one slot per letter
	isWord bool
}

func newTrie() Trie {
	return Trie{root: &trieNode{}}
}

func (t *Trie) insert(word string) {
	node := t.root
	for _, ch := range word {
		i := ch - 'a'
		if node.next[i] == nil {
			node.next[i] = &trieNode{}
		}
		node = node.next[i]
	}
	node.isWord = true
}

func (t *Trie) search(word string) bool {
	node := t.walk(word)
	return node != nil && node.isWord
}

func (t *Trie) startsWith(prefix string) bool {
	return t.walk(prefix) != nil
}

func (t *Trie) walk(s string) *trieNode { // follow s from the root, nil if it falls off
	node := t.root
	for _, ch := range s {
		node = node.next[ch-'a']
		if node == nil {
			return nil
		}
	}
	return node
}
struct TrieNode {
    next: [Option<Box<TrieNode>>; 26],           // one slot per letter
    is_word: bool,
}

impl TrieNode {
    fn new() -> Self {
        TrieNode { next: std::array::from_fn(|_| None), is_word: false }
    }
}

pub struct Trie {
    root: TrieNode,
}

impl Trie {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Trie { root: TrieNode::new() }
    }

    pub fn insert(&mut self, word: &str) {
        let mut node = &mut self.root;
        for ch in word.bytes() {
            let slot = (ch - b'a') as usize;
            node = node.next[slot].get_or_insert_with(|| Box::new(TrieNode::new()));
        }
        node.is_word = true;
    }

    pub fn search(&self, word: &str) -> bool {
        self.walk(word).is_some_and(|node| node.is_word)
    }

    pub fn starts_with(&self, prefix: &str) -> bool {
        self.walk(prefix).is_some()
    }

    fn walk(&self, s: &str) -> Option<&TrieNode> {   // follow s from root, None if it falls off
        let mut node = &self.root;
        for ch in s.bytes() {
            node = node.next[(ch - b'a') as usize].as_deref()?;
        }
        Some(node)
    }
}

Time O(L) per operation for a word of length L · Space O(total letters · 26)

Dijkstra

Trees & graphs less common

Use it when you need the shortest path, cheapest route or minimum time over weighted edges that are never negative: network delay, flight costs, minimum effort.

How it works

  • It's BFS with a min-heap ordered by distance in place of a plain queue.
  • Pop the closest node. If its distance is stale, skip it; otherwise relax each edge: if dist[u] + w < dist[v], update dist[v] and push it.
  • O((V + E) log V).

Watch out

  • Negative weights break it; use Bellman-Ford.
  • Heaps have no decrease-key, so push duplicates and skip the stale ones, as below.

Network Delay Time#743Medium

A signal starts at node k. How long until every node has it (-1 if some never do)?

// A binary heap, stored in an array. The children of slot i are
// 2i + 1 and 2i + 2, so the parent of slot i is (i - 1) / 2, rounded down.
class Heap<T> {
  private items: T[] = [];

  // compare works like sort's: (a, b) => a - b makes a min-heap.
  constructor(private compare: (a: T, b: T) => number) {}

  get size(): number {
    return this.items.length;
  }

  peek(): T | undefined {
    return this.items[0];
  }

  push(item: T): void {
    const a = this.items;
    a.push(item);    // add it at the end
    let i = a.length - 1;
    while (i > 0) {  // sift up while it beats its parent
      const parent = Math.floor((i - 1) / 2);
      if (this.compare(a[i], a[parent]) >= 0) break;
      [a[i], a[parent]] = [a[parent], a[i]];
      i = parent;
    }
  }

  pop(): T | undefined {
    const a = this.items;
    if (a.length <= 1) return a.pop();
    const top = a[0];
    a[0] = a.pop()!;  // move the last item to the top
    let i = 0;
    while (true) {    // sift down toward the better child
      let best = i;
      for (const kid of [2 * i + 1, 2 * i + 2])
        if (kid < a.length && this.compare(a[kid], a[best]) < 0) best = kid;
      if (best === i) return top;
      [a[i], a[best]] = [a[best], a[i]];
      i = best;
    }
  }
}

function networkDelayTime(times: number[][], n: number, k: number): number {
  const graph: [number, number][][] =
    Array.from({ length: n + 1 }, () => []);  // graph[u]: [v, time]
  for (const [from, to, time] of times) graph[from].push([to, time]);

  const dist: number[] = new Array(n + 1).fill(Infinity);
  dist[k] = 0;

  // [distance, node] pairs, the closest on top (the Heap from pattern 9)
  const heap = new Heap<[number, number]>((a, b) => a[0] - b[0]);
  heap.push([0, k]);

  while (heap.size > 0) {
    const [d, node] = heap.pop()!;
    if (d > dist[node]) continue;  // stale: settled cheaper already

    for (const [next, time] of graph[node]) {
      if (d + time >= dist[next]) continue;
      dist[next] = d + time;  // relax: a shorter way to next
      heap.push([dist[next], next]);
    }
  }

  const slowest = Math.max(...dist.slice(1));  // node 0 is unused
  return slowest === Infinity ? -1 : slowest;
}
def network_delay_time(times: list[list[int]], n: int, k: int) -> int:
    graph: list[list[tuple[int, int]]] = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for source, target, time in times:
        graph[source].append((target, time))

    dist: list[float] = [float("inf")] * (n + 1)
    dist[k] = 0

    heap: list[tuple[int, int]] = [(0, k)]     # (distance, node): priority is the distance

    while heap:
        d, node = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if d > dist[node]:
            continue                           # stale entry: already settled cheaper

        for nxt, time in graph[node]:
            if d + time >= dist[nxt]:
                continue
            dist[nxt] = d + time               # relax: a shorter way to next
            heapq.heappush(heap, (dist[nxt], nxt))

    slowest = max(dist[1:])                    # node 0 is unused
    return -1 if slowest == float("inf") else int(slowest)
public int networkDelayTime(int[][] times, int n, int k) {
    List<List<int[]>> graph = new ArrayList<>(n + 1);
    for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) graph.add(new ArrayList<>());
    for (int[] t : times) graph.get(t[0]).add(new int[] {t[1], t[2]});

    int[] dist = new int[n + 1];
    Arrays.fill(dist, Integer.MAX_VALUE);
    dist[k] = 0;

    // node, priority = distance
    PriorityQueue<int[]> heap = new PriorityQueue<>((a, b) -> a[1] - b[1]);
    heap.offer(new int[] {k, 0});

    while (!heap.isEmpty()) {
        int[] entry = heap.poll();
        int node = entry[0], d = entry[1];
        if (d > dist[node]) continue;          // stale entry: already settled cheaper

        for (int[] edge : graph.get(node)) {
            int next = edge[0], time = edge[1];
            if (d + time >= dist[next]) continue;
            dist[next] = d + time;             // relax: a shorter way to next
            heap.offer(new int[] {next, dist[next]});
        }
    }

    int slowest = Arrays.stream(dist, 1, n + 1).max().getAsInt();   // node 0 is unused
    return slowest == Integer.MAX_VALUE ? -1 : slowest;
}
public int NetworkDelayTime(int[][] times, int n, int k)
{
    var graph = new List<(int To, int Time)>[n + 1];
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) graph[i] = [];
    foreach (int[] t in times) graph[t[0]].Add((t[1], t[2]));

    var dist = new int[n + 1];
    Array.Fill(dist, int.MaxValue);
    dist[k] = 0;

    var heap = new PriorityQueue<int, int>();    // node, priority = distance
    heap.Enqueue(k, 0);

    while (heap.TryDequeue(out int node, out int d))
    {
        if (d > dist[node]) continue;            // stale entry: already settled cheaper

        foreach (var (next, time) in graph[node])
        {
            if (d + time >= dist[next]) continue;
            dist[next] = d + time;               // relax: a shorter way to next
            heap.Enqueue(next, dist[next]);
        }
    }

    int slowest = dist.Skip(1).Max();            // node 0 is unused
    return slowest == int.MaxValue ? -1 : slowest;
}
let networkDelayTime (times: int[][]) (n: int) (k: int) : int =
    let graph = Array.init (n + 1) (fun _ -> ResizeArray<int * int>())
    for t in times do graph[t[0]].Add((t[1], t[2]))

    let dist = Array.create (n + 1) Int32.MaxValue
    dist[k] <- 0

    let heap = PriorityQueue<int, int>()        // node, priority = distance
    heap.Enqueue(k, 0)

    let mutable node = 0
    let mutable d = 0
    while heap.TryDequeue(&node, &d) do
        if d <= dist[node] then                 // stale entry: already settled cheaper
            for (next, time) in graph[node] do
                if d + time < dist[next] then
                    dist[next] <- d + time      // relax: a shorter way to next
                    heap.Enqueue(next, dist[next])

    let mutable slowest = 0
    for i in 1 .. n do
        slowest <- max slowest dist[i]          // node 0 is unused

    if slowest = Int32.MaxValue then -1 else slowest
int networkDelayTime(vector<vector<int>>& times, int n, int k)
{
    vector<vector<pair<int, int>>> graph(n + 1);   // node -> (to, time)
    for (auto& t : times) graph[t[0]].push_back({t[1], t[2]});

    vector<int> dist(n + 1, INT_MAX);
    dist[k] = 0;

    priority_queue<pair<int, int>, vector<pair<int, int>>, greater<>> heap;   // (distance, node)
    heap.push({0, k});

    while (!heap.empty())
    {
        auto [d, node] = heap.top();
        heap.pop();
        if (d > dist[node]) continue;              // stale entry: already settled cheaper

        for (auto& [nxt, time] : graph[node])
        {
            if (d + time >= dist[nxt]) continue;
            dist[nxt] = d + time;                  // relax: a shorter way to next
            heap.push({dist[nxt], nxt});
        }
    }

    int slowest = *max_element(dist.begin() + 1, dist.end());   // node 0 is unused
    return slowest == INT_MAX ? -1 : slowest;
}
type edge struct {
	to, time int
}

// pathHeap orders nodes by the distance recorded when they were pushed.
type pathHeap [][2]int // {node, distance}

func (h pathHeap) Len() int           { return len(h) }
func (h pathHeap) Less(i, j int) bool { return h[i][1] < h[j][1] }
func (h pathHeap) Swap(i, j int)      { h[i], h[j] = h[j], h[i] }
func (h *pathHeap) Push(x any)        { *h = append(*h, x.([2]int)) }

func (h *pathHeap) Pop() any {
	old := *h
	n := len(old)
	item := old[n-1]
	*h = old[:n-1]
	return item
}

func networkDelayTime(times [][]int, n int, k int) int {
	graph := make([][]edge, n+1) // node 0 is unused
	for _, t := range times {
		graph[t[0]] = append(graph[t[0]], edge{t[1], t[2]})
	}

	dist := make([]int, n+1)
	for i := range dist {
		dist[i] = math.MaxInt
	}
	dist[k] = 0

	h := &pathHeap{{k, 0}} // {node, distance}
	heap.Init(h)

	for h.Len() > 0 {
		item := heap.Pop(h).([2]int)
		node, d := item[0], item[1]
		if d > dist[node] {
			continue // stale entry: already settled cheaper
		}

		for _, e := range graph[node] {
			if d+e.time >= dist[e.to] {
				continue
			}
			dist[e.to] = d + e.time // relax: a shorter way to next
			heap.Push(h, [2]int{e.to, dist[e.to]})
		}
	}

	slowest := 0
	for node := 1; node <= n; node++ { // node 0 is unused
		if dist[node] == math.MaxInt {
			return -1
		}
		slowest = max(slowest, dist[node])
	}
	return slowest
}
pub fn network_delay_time(times: &[Vec<i32>], n: i32, k: i32) -> i32 {
    let n = n as usize;
    let mut graph = vec![Vec::new(); n + 1];
    for t in times {
        graph[t[0] as usize].push((t[1] as usize, t[2]));
    }

    let mut dist = vec![i32::MAX; n + 1];
    dist[k as usize] = 0;

    let mut heap = BinaryHeap::new();            // (Reverse distance, node): nearest on top
    heap.push(Reverse((0, k as usize)));

    while let Some(Reverse((d, node))) = heap.pop() {
        if d > dist[node] { continue; }          // stale entry: already settled cheaper

        for &(next, time) in &graph[node] {
            if d + time >= dist[next] { continue; }
            dist[next] = d + time;               // relax: a shorter way to next
            heap.push(Reverse((dist[next], next)));
        }
    }

    let slowest = dist[1..].iter().copied().max().unwrap();   // node 0 is unused
    if slowest == i32::MAX { -1 } else { slowest }
}

Time O(E log E) · Space O(V + E)

func kitMaps() {
	// Map: count, look up, iterate
	count := map[rune]int{}
	for _, ch := range "banana" {
		count[ch]++ // missing keys read as 0
	}

	if n, found := count['a']; found { // one lookup, never panics
		fmt.Println("a appears", n, "times")
	}
	delete(count, 'b')
	for ch, value := range count { // map order is random, not insertion order
		fmt.Printf("%c: %d\n", ch, value)
	}

	// Set: membership in O(1), and the empty struct stores nothing
	seen := map[int]struct{}{}
	seen[42] = struct{}{}
	_, has := seen[42] // false when 42 was never added
	fmt.Println(has)
}
pub fn kit_maps() {
    // HashMap: count, look up, iterate
    let mut count: HashMap<char, usize> = HashMap::new();
    for ch in "banana".chars() {
        *count.entry(ch).or_insert(0) += 1;      // entry() reads a missing key as 0
    }

    let found = count.get(&'a').copied();        // one lookup, an Option, never panics
    count.remove(&'b');
    for (key, value) in &count {                 // iterate by reference
        println!("{key}: {value}");
    }

    // HashSet: membership in O(1)
    let mut seen: HashSet<i32> = HashSet::new();
    let is_new = seen.insert(42);                // false if 42 was already there
    let has = seen.contains(&42);
}

// A binary heap, stored in an array. The children of slot i are
// 2i + 1 and 2i + 2, so the parent of slot i is (i - 1) / 2, rounded down.
class Heap<T> {
  private items: T[] = [];

  // compare works like sort's: (a, b) => a - b makes a min-heap.
  constructor(private compare: (a: T, b: T) => number) {}

  get size(): number {
    return this.items.length;
  }

  peek(): T | undefined {
    return this.items[0];
  }

  push(item: T): void {
    const a = this.items;
    a.push(item);    // add it at the end
    let i = a.length - 1;
    while (i > 0) {  // sift up while it beats its parent
      const parent = Math.floor((i - 1) / 2);
      if (this.compare(a[i], a[parent]) >= 0) break;
      [a[i], a[parent]] = [a[parent], a[i]];
      i = parent;
    }
  }

  pop(): T | undefined {
    const a = this.items;
    if (a.length <= 1) return a.pop();
    const top = a[0];
    a[0] = a.pop()!;  // move the last item to the top
    let i = 0;
    while (true) {    // sift down toward the better child
      let best = i;
      for (const kid of [2 * i + 1, 2 * i + 2])
        if (kid < a.length && this.compare(a[kid], a[best]) < 0) best = kid;
      if (best === i) return top;
      [a[i], a[best]] = [a[best], a[i]];
      i = best;
    }
  }
}

{

    st.push(1);
    int top = st.top();                            // check !st.empty() first
    st.pop();

    queue<pair<int, int>> q;                       // pairs are handy for grids
    q.push({0, 0});
    auto [row, col] = q.front();
    q.pop();

    // priority_queue is a max-heap by default; greater<> flips it to a min-heap
    priority_queue<pair<int, string>, vector<pair<int, string>>, greater<>> minHeap;
    minHeap.push({2, "write tests"});              // (priority, element)
    minHeap.push({1, "fix bug"});
    string first = minHeap.top().second;           // "fix bug": lowest priority first
    minHeap.pop();

    // A plain int queue is the other way round: the default is already a max-heap
    priority_queue<int> maxHeap;
    maxHeap.push(3);
    maxHeap.push(9);
    int largest = maxHeap.top();

    cout << top << ' ' << row << ',' << col << ' ' << first << ' ' << largest << "\n";

// intHeap is a min-heap of ints; set max for a max-heap.
type intHeap struct {
	items []int
	max   bool
}

func (h intHeap) Len() int { return len(h.items) }
func (h intHeap) Less(i, j int) bool {
	if h.max {
		return h.items[i] > h.items[j]
	}
	return h.items[i] < h.items[j]
}
func (h intHeap) Swap(i, j int) { h.items[i], h.items[j] = h.items[j], h.items[i] }
func (h *intHeap) Push(x any)   { h.items = append(h.items, x.(int)) }

func (h *intHeap) Pop() any {
	n := len(h.items) - 1
	x := h.items[n]
	h.items = h.items[:n]
	return x
}

	maxHeap := &intHeap{max: true} // reversed: a max-heap
	heap.Init(maxHeap)
	heap.Push(maxHeap, 5)
	heap.Push(maxHeap, 9)
	fmt.Println(heap.Pop(maxHeap)) // 9: highest value first
}
pub fn kit_collections() {
    // Vec is LIFO, VecDeque is FIFO
    let mut stack = Vec::new();
    stack.push(1);
    let top = stack.last();                      // an Option: check is_some() first
    stack.pop();

    let mut queue: VecDeque<(i32, i32)> = VecDeque::new();   // tuples are handy for grids
    queue.push_back((0, 0));
    let (row, col) = queue.pop_front().unwrap();

    // BinaryHeap is a max-heap; Reverse turns the comparison around
    let mut min_heap: BinaryHeap<Reverse<(i32, &str)>> = BinaryHeap::new();   // (priority, item)
    min_heap.push(Reverse((2, "write tests")));
    min_heap.push(Reverse((1, "fix bug")));
    let Reverse((_, first)) = min_heap.pop().unwrap();   // "fix bug": lowest priority first

    let max_heap: BinaryHeap<i32> = BinaryHeap::new();   // plain ordering: largest on top
}

// No built-in binary search: write the lower bound yourself
function lowerBound(a: number[], target: number): number {
  let lo = 0, hi = a.length;
  while (lo < hi) {
    const mid = (lo + hi) >> 1;
    if (a[mid] < target) lo = mid + 1;
    else hi = mid;
  }
  return lo;
}

func kitArrays() {
	nums := []int{5, 2, 9}
	sort.Ints(nums)                              // ascending, in place
	sort.Sort(sort.Reverse(sort.IntSlice(nums))) // descending
	pairs := [][]int{{3, 1}, {1, 2}}
	sort.Slice(pairs, func(i, j int) bool { return pairs[i][0] < pairs[j][0] }) // by first element

	table := make([][]int, 3) // fixed 2D grid: table[r][c]
	for r := range table {
		table[r] = make([]int, 4)
	}
	memo := make([]int, 10)
	for i := range memo {
		memo[i] = -1
	}
	last := nums[len(nums)-1]       // index from the end
	middle := nums[1 : len(nums)-1] // slice (a view, not a copy)
	fmt.Println(last, middle, table[2][3])

	list := []int{4, 1, 3}
	sort.Ints(list)
	at := sort.SearchInts(list, 3) // where 3 is or would go: list[at] == 3 when found
	fmt.Println(at)
}
pub fn kit_arrays() {
    let mut nums = vec![5, 2, 9];
    nums.sort();                                 // ascending, in place
    nums.sort_by(|a, b| b.cmp(a));                // descending
    let mut pairs = vec![[3, 1], [1, 2]];
    pairs.sort_by_key(|pair| pair[0]);           // by first element

    let table = vec![vec![0; 4]; 3];              // fixed 2D grid: table[r][c]
    let mut memo = [0; 10];
    memo.fill(-1);
    let last = nums[nums.len() - 1];             // index from the end
    let middle = &nums[1..nums.len() - 1];       // a slice, borrowed rather than copied

    let mut list = vec![4, 1, 3];
    list.sort();
    let at = list.binary_search(&3);             // Ok(index) when found
}

void kitStrings()
{
    string s = "leetcode";
    vector<int> freq(26, 0);
    for (char ch : s) freq[ch - 'a']++;            // 'a'..'z' -> 0..25

    string reversed(s.rbegin(), s.rend());

    string built;                                  // build strings in loops
    for (char ch : string("abc")) built += ch;

    int digit = '7' - '0';                         // char digit -> int

    istringstream in("a b c");
    vector<string> parts{istream_iterator<string>(in), istream_iterator<string>()};
    string joined;
    for (auto& part : parts) joined += (joined.empty() ? "" : ",") + part;

    int lo = 0, hi = 100;
    int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;                  // midpoint that can't overflow
    long long product = 1LL * hi * hi;             // widen before multiplying
    int hours = (7 + 2 - 1) / 2;                   // ceiling of 7 / 2
    int mod = ((-7 % 3) + 3) % 3;                  // % keeps the sign of the left side

    cout << freq['e' - 'a'] << ' ' << reversed << ' ' << built << ' ' << digit
         << ' ' << joined << ' ' << mid << ' ' << product << ' ' << hours
         << ' ' << mod << "\n";
}
func kitStrings() {
	s := "leetcode"
	freq := make([]int, 26)
	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
		freq[s[i]-'a']++ // 'a'..'z' -> 0..25
	}

	chars := []byte(s)
	for i, j := 0, len(chars)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
		chars[i], chars[j] = chars[j], chars[i]
	}
	reversed := string(chars)

	var sb strings.Builder // build strings in loops
	sb.WriteString("ab")
	sb.WriteByte('c')
	built := sb.String()

	digit := '7' - '0' // char digit -> int
	joined := strings.Join(strings.Split("a b c", " "), ",")

	lo, hi := 0, 100
	mid := lo + (hi-lo)/2            // midpoint that can't overflow
	product := int64(hi) * int64(hi) // widen before multiplying
	hours := (7 + 2 - 1) / 2         // ceiling of 7 / 2
	mod := ((-7 % 3) + 3) % 3        // Go's % keeps the sign of the dividend

	fmt.Println(freq[0], reversed, built, digit, joined, mid, product, hours, mod)
}
pub fn kit_strings() {
    let s = "leetcode";
    let mut freq = [0usize; 26];
    for ch in s.bytes() {
        freq[(ch - b'a') as usize] += 1;         // b'a'..=b'z' -> 0..=25
    }

    let reversed: String = s.chars().rev().collect();

    let mut built = String::new();               // build strings in loops
    built.push_str("ab");
    built.push('c');

    let digit = ('7' as u8 - b'0') as i32;       // char digit -> int
    let joined = "a b c".split(' ').collect::<Vec<_>>().join(",");

    let (lo, hi) = (0, 100);
    let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;                // midpoint that cannot overflow
    let product = (hi as i64) * (hi as i64);     // widen before multiplying
    let hours = (7 + 2 - 1) / 2;                 // ceiling of 7 / 2
    let modulo = ((-7 % 3) + 3) % 3;             // Rust % can be negative
}

// LeetCode supplies these for linked list and tree problems.
class ListNode {
  val: number;
  next: ListNode | null;

  constructor(val = 0, next: ListNode | null = null) {
    this.val = val;
    this.next = next;
  }
}

class TreeNode {
  val: number;
  left: TreeNode | null;
  right: TreeNode | null;

  constructor(val = 0, left: TreeNode | null = null, right: TreeNode | null = null) {
    this.val = val;
    this.left = left;
    this.right = right;
  }
}

Study plan

  1. Take one pattern at a time. Read the card, close it, and write both examples from memory.
  2. Then work through its "Practice next" list. Give each problem 25 minutes; if you're stuck, read a solution, name the signal you missed, and solve it again from scratch.
  3. Solve each problem again three days later and once more after a week. The second attempt is what sticks.
  4. Say the trigger out loud when you read a new problem: "k largest, so a heap of size k".
  5. Leave dynamic programming for last and give it the most time: recursion first, then a memo, then a table.
  6. In the dojo, keep the README loop: explain the approach, implement in Solution.cs, run the tests, then state the complexity.
Every snippet compiles in TypeScript, Python, Java, C#, F#, C++, Go and Rust, and the C# versions also pass LeetCode's sample cases (checked October 28, 2026). Diagrams were drawn in draw.io and PlantUML; each figure's source and step data are embedded beside it.
